vinā snānaṃ tu yatkarma puṇyakāryamayaṃ śubham ..
kriyate niṣphalaṃ brahmaṃstatpragṛhṇaṃti rākṣasāḥ ..28..
5.232.d:
विना स्नानं तु यत्कर्म पुण्यकार्यमयं शुभम् ..
क्रियते निष्फलं ब्रह्मंस्तत्प्रगृह्णंति राक्षसाः ..28..
5.232.m:
Whatever rite, consisting of holy works and auspicious, is performed without ritual ablution
becomes fruitless, O brahmin; the rākṣasas seize it. (28)

5.232.s:
snānena satyamāpnoti snānaṃ dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ ..
dharmānmokṣaphalaṃ prāpya punarnaivāvasīdati..29..
ye cādhyātmavidaḥ puṇyā ye ca vedāṃgapāragāḥ ..
sarvadānapradā ye ca teṣāṃ snānena śuddhatā ..6.233.3...
5.232.d:
स्नानेन सत्यमाप्नोति स्नानं धर्मः सनातनः ..
धर्मान्मोक्षफलं प्राप्य पुनर्नैवावसीदति..29..
ये चाध्यात्मविदः पुण्या ये च वेदांगपारगाः ..
सर्वदानप्रदा ये च तेषां स्नानेन शुद्धता ..6.233.3...
5.232.m:
Through ritual ablution one attains truth; ritual ablution is eternal duty;
attaining the fruit of liberation through duty, one never suffers again. (29)
Those holy men who know the supreme Self, those who have mastered the Vedāṅgas,
and those who give every gift—their purification comes through ritual ablution. (30)

5.232.s:
kṛtasnānasya ca harirdehamāśritya tiṣṭhati ..
sarvakriyākalāpeṣu saṃpūrṇa phalado bhavet .. 31 ..
5.232.d:
कृतस्नानस्य च हरिर्देहमाश्रित्य तिष्ठति ..
सर्वक्रियाकलापेषु संपूर्ण फलदो भवेत् .. 31 ..
5.232.m:
And Hari resides in the body of one who has performed ritual ablution;
he bestows the full fruit in all collections of rituals. (31)

5.232.s:
sarvapāpavināśāya devatā toṣaṇāya ca ..
cāturmāsye jalasnānaṃ sarvapāpakṣayāvaham .. 32 ..
5.232.d:
सर्वपापविनाशाय देवता तोषणाय च ..
चातुर्मास्ये जलस्नानं सर्वपापक्षयावहम् .. 32 ..
5.232.m:
For the destruction of all sins and the propitiation of the deity,
ritual ablution in water during Cāturmāsya brings about the destruction of all sins. (32)

5.232.s:
niśāyāṃ caiva na snāyātsaṃdhyāyāṃ grahaṇaṃ vinā ..
uṣṇodakena na snānaṃ rātrau śuddhirna jāyate .. 33 ..
5.232.d:
निशायां चैव न स्नायात्संध्यायां ग्रहणं विना ..
उष्णोदकेन न स्नानं रात्रौ शुद्धिर्न जायते .. 33 ..
5.232.m:
One should not bathe at night, nor at twilight, except during an eclipse;
ritual ablution is not done with hot water; purification does not occur at night. (33)

5.232.s:
bhānusaṃdarśanācchuddhirvihitā sarvakarmasu ..
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa jalaśuddhistu bhāvinī .. 34 ..
5.232.d:
भानुसंदर्शनाच्छुद्धिर्विहिता सर्वकर्मसु ..
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण जलशुद्धिस्तु भाविनी .. 34 ..
5.232.m:
Purification is prescribed in all rituals by looking upon the sun;
especially during Cāturmāsya, the purification of water will surely occur. (34)

5.232.s:
aśaktyā tu śarīrasya bhasmasnānena śudhyati ..
maṃtrasnānena vipreṃdra viṣṇupādodakena vā .. 358 ..
nārāyaṇāgrataḥ snānaṃ kṣetra tīrthanadīṣu ca ..
yaḥ karoti viśuddhātmā cāturmāsye viśeṣataḥ .. 36 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne cāturmāsyamāhātmye brahmanāradasaṃvāde gaṃgodakasnānaphalamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma trayastriṃśaduttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ..233.... ..
5.232.d:
अशक्त्या तु शरीरस्य भस्मस्नानेन शुध्यति ..
मंत्रस्नानेन विप्रेंद्र विष्णुपादोदकेन वा .. 358 ..
नारायणाग्रतः स्नानं क्षेत्र तीर्थनदीषु च ..
यः करोति विशुद्धात्मा चातुर्मास्ये विशेषतः .. 36 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे गंगोदकस्नानफलमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम त्रयस्त्रिंशदुत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः..233.... ..
5.232.m:
In case of physical incapacity, one is purified by ash-ablution,
by mantra-ablution, O chief of brahmins, or by Viṣṇu's foot-wash water. (35)
One of purified soul who performs ritual ablution before Nārāyaṇa,
in sacred fields, sacred fords, and rivers, especially during Cāturmāsya— (36)
Thus ends the two hundred and thirty-third chapter, entitled 'Description of the Greatness of the Fruit of Bathing in Gaṅgā Water,' in the conversation between Brahmā and Nārada, within the Greatness of Cāturmāsya, in the narrative of Him Who Reclines on Śeṣa, in the Greatness of Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the sixth Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the venerable Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.233.s:
brahmovāca .. ..
pitṝṇāṃ tarpaṇaṃ kuryācchraddhāyuktena cetasā ..
snānāvasāne nityaṃ ca gupte deve mahāphalam ..1..
5.233.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच .. ..
पितॄणां तर्पणं कुर्याच्छ्रद्धायुक्तेन चेतसा ..
स्नानावसाने नित्यं च गुप्ते देवे महाफलम् ..1..
5.233.m: Brahmā said: / One should offer libations to the ancestors with a devout mind / at the conclusion of ritual ablution daily; while the god is concealed, it brings great fruit. (1)

5.233.s:
saṃgame saritostatra pitṝnsaṃtarpya devatāḥ ..
japahomādikarmāṇi kṛtvā phalamanaṃtakam ..2..
5.233.d:
संगमे सरितोस्तत्र पितॄन्संतर्प्य देवताः ..
जपहोमादिकर्माणि कृत्वा फलमनंतकम् ..2..
5.233.m: Having offered libations there to the ancestors and gods at the confluence of two rivers, / and having performed rites such as recitation and fire offerings, one attains endless fruit. (2)

5.233.s:
goviṃdasmaraṇaṃ kṛtvā paścātkāryāḥ śubhāḥ kriyāḥ ..
eṣa eva pitṛdevamanuṣyādiṣu tṛptidaḥ .. 3 ..
5.233.d:
गोविंदस्मरणं कृत्वा पश्चात्कार्याः शुभाः क्रियाः ..
एष एव पितृदेवमनुष्यादिषु तृप्तिदः .. 3 ..
5.233.m: Having remembered Govinda, auspicious rites should then be performed; / this alone gives satisfaction to ancestors, gods, men, and others. (3)

5.233.s:
śraddhāṃ dharmayutāṃ nāma smṛtipūtāni kārayet ..
karmāṇi sakalānīha cāturmāsye guṇottare .. 4 ..
5.233.d:
श्रद्धां धर्मयुतां नाम स्मृतिपूतानि कारयेत् ..
कर्माणि सकलानीह चातुर्मास्ये गुणोत्तरे .. 4 ..
5.233.m: Endowed with faith and righteousness, one should perform all rites / purified by the smṛtis here during Cāturmāsya, which is supreme in virtues. (4)

5.233.s:
satsaṃgo dvijabhaktiśca gurudevāgni tarpaṇam ..
gopradānaṃ vedapāṭhaḥ satkriyāsatyabhāṣaṇam .. 5 ..
5.233.d:
सत्संगो द्विजभक्तिश्च गुरुदेवाग्नि तर्पणम् ..
गोप्रदानं वेदपाठः सत्क्रियासत्यभाषणम् .. 5 ..
5.233.m: Association with the virtuous, devotion to the twice-born, propitiating the guru, gods, and fire, / the gift of cows, recitation of the Veda, right action, and speaking the truth; (5)

5.233.s:
gobhaktirdānabhaktiśca sadā dharmasya sādhanam ..
kṛṣṇe supte viśeṣeṇa niyamo'pi mahā phalaḥ .. 6 ..
5.233.d:
गोभक्तिर्दानभक्तिश्च सदा धर्मस्य साधनम् ..
कृष्णे सुप्ते विशेषेण नियमोऽपि महा फलः .. 6 ..
5.233.m: devotion to cows and devotion to charity are always the means to righteousness; / especially while Kṛṣṇa is asleep, observance of vows also yields great fruit. (6)

5.233.s:
.. nārada uvāca .. ..
niyamaḥ kīdṛśo brahmanphalaṃ ca niyamena kim ..
niyamena haristuṣṭo yathā bhavati tadvada ..7 ..
5.233.d:
.. नारद उवाच .. ..
नियमः कीदृशो ब्रह्मन्फलं च नियमेन किम् ..
नियमेन हरिस्तुष्टो यथा भवति तद्वद ..7 ..
5.233.m: Nārada said: / What kind of observance is it, O Brahmā, and what is the fruit of that observance? / Speak that by which observance Hari becomes pleased. (7)

5.233.s:
.. brahmovāca .. ..
niyamaścakṣurādīnāṃ kriyāsu vividhāsu ca ..
kāryo vidyāvatā puṃsā tatprayogānmahāsukham .. 8 ..
5.233.d:
.. ब्रह्मोवाच .. ..
नियमश्चक्षुरादीनां क्रियासु विविधासु च ..
कार्यो विद्यावता पुंसा तत्प्रयोगान्महासुखम् .. 8 ..
5.233.m: Brahmā said: / The restraint of the eyes and other senses in various actions / should be practiced by an educated man; from its practice comes great happiness. (8)

5.233.s:
etatṣaḍvargaharaṇaṃ ripunigrahaṇaṃ param ..
adhyātmamūlametaddhi paramaṃ saukhyakāraṇam .. 9 ..
5.233.d:
एतत्षड्वर्गहरणं रिपुनिग्रहणं परम् ..
अध्यात्ममूलमेतद्धि परमं सौख्यकारणम् .. 9 ..
5.233.m: This is the destruction of the six enemies, the supreme subjugation of foes; / this indeed is the root of spirituality and the supreme cause of happiness. (9)

5.233.s:
tatra tiṣṭhaṃti niyataṃ kṣamāsatyādayo guṇāḥ ..
vivekarūpiṇaḥ sarve tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam .. 6.234.10 ..
5.233.d:
तत्र तिष्ठंति नियतं क्षमासत्यादयो गुणाः ..
विवेकरूपिणः सर्वे तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् .. 6.234.10 ..
5.233.m: There virtues such as forbearance and truth always dwell, / all taking the form of discrimination; that is Viṣṇu's supreme state. (10)

5.233.s:
kṛtvā bhavati yajñānyatkṛtakṛtyatvamatra tat ..
syāttasya tatpūrvajānāṃ yena jñātamidaṃ padam .. 11 ..
5.233.d:
कृत्वा भवति यज्ञान्यत्कृतकृत्यत्वमत्र तत् ..
स्यात्तस्य तत्पूर्वजानां येन ज्ञातमिदं पदम् .. 11 ..
5.233.m: Having done this, whatever other sacrifice is performed, fulfillment of duty is achieved; / it accrues to him and to his ancestors, by whom this state has been known. (11)

5.233.s:
tanmuhūrttamapi dhyātvā pāpaṃ janmaśatodbhavam..
bhasma sādyāti vihitaṃ niraṃjananiṣevaṇāt .. 12 ..
5.233.d:
तन्मुहूर्त्तमपि ध्यात्वा पापं जन्मशतोद्भवम्..
भस्म साद्याति विहितं निरंजननिषेवणात् .. 12 ..
5.233.m: Meditating on that even for a moment, sin arising from hundreds of births / goes to ashes, duly destroyed through serving the taintless one. (12)

5.233.s:
pratyahaṃ saṃkucatyasya kṣutpipāsādikaḥ śramaḥ ..
sa yogī niyamī nityaṃ harau supte viśiṣyate .. 13 ..
5.233.d:
प्रत्यहं संकुचत्यस्य क्षुत्पिपासादिकः श्रमः ..
स योगी नियमी नित्यं हरौ सुप्ते विशिष्यते .. 13 ..
5.233.m: Day by day, the exhaustion of hunger, thirst, and the like shrinks away for him; / that yogin, constantly observant of vows, is distinguished while Hari is asleep. (13)

5.233.s:
cāturmāsye naro bhaktyā yogābhyāsarato na cet ..
tasya hastātparibhraṣṭamamṛtaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 14 ..
5.233.d:
चातुर्मास्ये नरो भक्त्या योगाभ्यासरतो न चेत् ..
तस्य हस्तात्परिभ्रष्टममृतं नात्र संशयः .. 14 ..
5.233.m: If a man does not devotedly engage in the practice of yoga during Cāturmāsya, / nectar has slipped from his hand; of this there is no doubt. (14)

5.233.s:
mano niyamitaṃ yena sarvecchāsu sadāgatam..
tasya jñāne ca mokṣe ca kāraṇaṃ mana eva hi .. 15 ..
5.233.d:
मनो नियमितं येन सर्वेच्छासु सदागतम्..
तस्य ज्ञाने च मोक्षे च कारणं मन एव हि .. 15 ..
5.233.m: By whom the mind, which always wanders among all desires, is restrained, / for him that very mind is the cause of knowledge and liberation. (15)

5.233.s:
manoniyamane yatnaḥ kāryaḥ prajñāvatā sadā ..
manasā sugṛhītena jñānāptirakhilā dhruvam .. 16 ..
5.233.d:
मनोनियमने यत्नः कार्यः प्रज्ञावता सदा ..
मनसा सुगृहीतेन ज्ञानाप्तिरखिला ध्रुवम् .. 16 ..
5.233.m: Effort in restraining the mind should always be made by a wise man; / when the mind is well restrained, all knowledge is certainly attained. (16)

5.233.s:
tanmanaḥ kṣamayā grāhyaṃ yathā vahniśca vāriṇā ..
ekayā kṣamayā sarvo niyamaḥ kathito budhaiḥ .. 17 ..
5.233.d:
तन्मनः क्षमया ग्राह्यं यथा वह्निश्च वारिणा ..
एकया क्षमया सर्वो नियमः कथितो बुधैः .. 17 ..
5.233.m: That mind is to be seized with forbearance, just as fire is controlled by water; / through forbearance alone is all restraint declared by the wise. (17)

5.233.s:
satyamekaṃ paro dharmaḥ satyamekaṃ paraṃ tapaḥ ..
satyamekaṃ paraṃ jñānaṃ satye dharmaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ .. 18 ..
5.233.d:
सत्यमेकं परो धर्मः सत्यमेकं परं तपः ..
सत्यमेकं परं ज्ञानं सत्ये धर्मः प्रतिष्ठितः .. 18 ..
5.233.m: Truth alone is the highest dharma; truth alone is the supreme austerity. / Truth alone is supreme knowledge; dharma is established upon truth.

5.233.s:
dharmamūlamahiṃsā ca manasā tāṃ ca citayan ..
karmaṇā ca tathā vācā tata etāṃ samācaret .. 19 ..
5.233.d:
धर्ममूलमहिंसा च मनसा तां च चितयन् ..
कर्मणा च तथा वाचा तत एतां समाचरेत् .. 19 ..
5.233.m: And non-violence is the root of dharma: contemplating it in thought, / and likewise in deed and in speech, one should then practice it.

5.233.s:
parasvaharaṇaṃ cauryaṃ sarvadā sarvamānuṣaiḥ ..
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa brahmadevasvavarjanam .. 6.234.20 ..
5.233.d:
परस्वहरणं चौर्यं सर्वदा सर्वमानुषैः ..
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण ब्रह्मदेवस्ववर्जनम् .. 6.234.20 ..
5.233.m: Taking another's property is theft at all times for all men; / especially during the Cāturmāsya, the avoidance of property belonging to brahmins and gods [is enjoined].

5.233.s:
akṛtyakaraṇaṃ caiva varjanīyaṃ sadā budhaiḥ ..
ahīnaḥ sarvakāryeṣu yaḥ sadā vipra vartate .. 21 ..
5.233.d:
अकृत्यकरणं चैव वर्जनीयं सदा बुधैः ..
अहीनः सर्वकार्येषु यः सदा विप्र वर्तते .. 21 ..
5.233.m: And the performance of improper deeds must always be avoided by the wise. / The one who always remains untainted in all actions, O brahmin,

5.233.s:
sa ca yogī mahāprājñaḥ prajñācakṣurahaṃ nadhīḥ .. ?
ahaṃkāro viṣamidaṃ śarīre varttate nṛṇām .. 22 ..
5.233.d:
स च योगी महाप्राज्ञः प्रज्ञाचक्षुरहं नधीः .. ?
अहंकारो विषमिदं शरीरे वर्त्तते नृणाम् .. 22 ..
5.233.m: that yogin is great in wisdom, possessing the eye of wisdom, devoid of the notion of ego. / This egoism exists as a poison in the body of men;

5.233.s:
tasmātsa sarvadā tyājyaḥ supte deve viśeṣataḥ ..
anīhayā jitakrodho jitalobho bhavennaraḥ .. 23 ..
5.233.d:
तस्मात्स सर्वदा त्याज्यः सुप्ते देवे विशेषतः ..
अनीहया जितक्रोधो जितलोभो भवेन्नरः .. 23 ..
5.233.m: therefore it must always be abandoned, especially while the God is asleep. / Through freedom from craving, a person should overcome anger and overcome greed.

5.233.s:
tasya pāpasahasrāṇi dehādyāṃti sahasradhā ..
mohaṃ mānaṃ parājitya śamarūpeṇa śatruṇā .. 24 ..
5.233.d:
तस्य पापसहस्राणि देहाद्यांति सहस्रधा ..
मोहं मानं पराजित्य शमरूपेण शत्रुणा .. 24 ..
5.233.m: His thousands of sins depart from the body in a thousand ways. / Having conquered delusion and pride through peace, the enemy [of passions],

5.233.s:
vicāreṇa śamo grāhyaḥ santoṣeṇa tathā hi saḥ ..
mātsaryamṛjubhāvena niyacchetsa munīśvaraḥ .. 25 ..
5.233.d:
विचारेण शमो ग्राह्यः सन्तोषेण तथा हि सः ..
मात्सर्यमृजुभावेन नियच्छेत्स मुनीश्वरः .. 25 ..
5.233.m: peace is to be grasped through reflection, and likewise through contentment. / By means of straightforwardness, that lord among sages should restrain malice.

5.233.s:
cāturmāsye dayādharmo na dharmo bhūtavidruhām ..
sarvadā sarva dāneṣu bhūtadrohaṃ vivarjayet .. 26 ..
5.233.d:
चातुर्मास्ये दयाधर्मो न धर्मो भूतविद्रुहाम् ..
सर्वदा सर्व दानेषु भूतद्रोहं विवर्जयेत् .. 26 ..
5.233.m: During the Cāturmāsya, the dharma of compassion [holds]; there is no dharma for those who harm living beings. / In all gifts at all times, one should shun malice toward creatures.

5.233.s:
etatpāpasahasrāṇāṃ mūlaṃ prāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ ..
tasmātsarvaprayatnena kāryā bhūtadayā nṛbhiḥ .. 27 ..
5.233.d:
एतत्पापसहस्राणां मूलं प्राहुर्मनीषिणः ..
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन कार्या भूतदया नृभिः .. 27 ..
5.233.m: Wise men call this the root of thousands of sins; / therefore, with every effort, compassion for creatures must be practiced by men.

5.233.s:
sarveṣāmeva bhūtānāṃ harirnityaṃ hṛdi sthitaḥ ..
sa eva hi parābhūto yo bhūtadrohakārakaḥ .. 28 ..
5.233.d:
सर्वेषामेव भूतानां हरिर्नित्यं हृदि स्थितः ..
स एव हि पराभूतो यो भूतद्रोहकारकः .. 28 ..
5.233.m: Hari is constantly present in the hearts of all beings indeed. / He alone is truly humiliated who causes harm to creatures.

5.233.s:
yasmindharme dayā naiva sa dharmo dūṣito mataḥ ..
dayāṃ vinā na vijñānaṃ na dharmo jñānameva ca .. 29 ..
5.233.d:
यस्मिन्धर्मे दया नैव स धर्मो दूषितो मतः ..
दयां विना न विज्ञानं न धर्मो ज्ञानमेव च .. 29 ..
5.233.m: That dharma in which there is no compassion is considered flawed; / without compassion there is neither discernment nor dharma nor true knowledge.

5.233.s:
tasmātsarvātmabhāvena dayādharmaḥ sanātanaḥ ..
sevyaḥ sa puruṣairnityaṃ cāturmāsye viśeṣataḥ .. 6.234.30 ..
5.233.d:
तस्मात्सर्वात्मभावेन दयाधर्मः सनातनः ..
सेव्यः स पुरुषैर्नित्यं चातुर्मास्ये विशेषतः .. 6.234.30 ..
5.233.m: Therefore, with one's whole soul, the eternal dharma of compassion / should constantly be cultivated by people, especially during the Cāturmāsya.

5.233.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye cāturmāsyamāhātmye śepaśāyyupākhyāne brahma nāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsyaniyamavidhimāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma catustriṃśaduttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 234 ..
5.233.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये शेपशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्म नारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्यनियमविधिमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम चतुस्त्रिंशदुत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः .. 234 ..
5.233.m: Thus ends the two hundred and thirty-fourth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Glory of the Observances of the Rules of Cāturmāsya', in the narrative of the one lying on the couch, in the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada, in the Glory of Cāturmāsya, in the Glory of Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the sixth Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the venerable Skanda Mahāpurāṇa comprising eighty-one thousand verses.

5.234.s:
.. brahmovāca .. ..
dānadharmaṃ praśaṃsaṃti sarvadharmeṣu sarvadā ..
harau supte viśeṣeṇa dānaṃ brahmatvakāraṇam .. 1 ..
5.234.d:
.. ब्रह्मोवाच .. ..
दानधर्मं प्रशंसंति सर्वधर्मेषु सर्वदा ..
हरौ सुप्ते विशेषेण दानं ब्रह्मत्वकारणम् .. 1 ..
5.234.m: Brahmā said: / They always praise the dharma of giving among all dharmas; / especially while Hari is asleep, giving is the cause of attainment to Brahman.

5.234.s:
annaṃ brahma iti proktamanne prāṇāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ ..
tasmādannaprado nityaṃ vāridaśca bhavennaraḥ .. 2 ..
5.234.d:
अन्नं ब्रह्म इति प्रोक्तमन्ने प्राणाः प्रतिष्ठिताः ..
तस्मादन्नप्रदो नित्यं वारिदश्च भवेन्नरः .. 2 ..
5.234.m: Food is declared to be Brahman; upon food the life-breaths are established. / Therefore, a person should constantly be a giver of food and a giver of water.

5.234.s:
vāridastṛptimāyāti sukhamakṣayyamannadaḥ ..
vāryannayoḥ samaṃ dānaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati .. 3 ..
5.234.d:
वारिदस्तृप्तिमायाति सुखमक्षय्यमन्नदः ..
वार्यन्नयोः समं दानं न भूतं न भविष्यति .. 3 ..
5.234.m: The giver of water attains satisfaction; the giver of food attains imperishable happiness. / Equal to the gift of water and food there has not been nor will there ever be.

5.234.s:
maṇiratnapravālānāṃ rūpyaṃ hāṭakavāsasām..
anyeṣāmapi dānānāmannadānaṃ viśiṣyate .. 4 ..
5.234.d:
मणिरत्नप्रवालानां रूप्यं हाटकवाससाम्..
अन्येषामपि दानानामन्नदानं विशिष्यते .. 4 ..
5.234.m: Compared to gifts of jewels, gems, corals, silver, gold, and garments, / and compared even to other gifts, the gift of food is pre-eminent.

5.234.s:
annodakapradānaṃ ca gopradānaṃ ca nityadā ..
vedapāṭho vahnihomaścāturmāsye mahāphalam .. 9 ..
vaikuṇṭhapadavāñchā cedviṣṇunā saha saṃgame ..
sarvapāpakṣayārthāya cāturmāsye'nnado bhavet .. 6 ..
satyaṃsatyaṃ hi devarṣe mayoktaṃ tava nārada ..
janmāṃtarasahasreṣu nādattamupatiṣṭhate .. 7 ..
tasmādannapradānena sarve hṛṣyaṃti jantavaḥ ..
devāśca spṛhayaṃtyenamannadānapradāyinam .. 8 ..
ājyaṃ deyaṃ ca pātreṣu śraddhayā vajramiśritam ..
vajradānakaro martyaścāturmāsye na mānavaḥ .. 9 ..
5.234.d:
अन्नोदकप्रदानं च गोप्रदानं च नित्यदा ..
वेदपाठो वह्निहोमश्चातुर्मास्ये महाफलम् .. 9 ..
वैकुण्ठपदवाञ्छा चेद्विष्णुना सह संगमे ..
सर्वपापक्षयार्थाय चातुर्मास्येऽन्नदो भवेत् .. 6 ..
सत्यंसत्यं हि देवर्षे मयोक्तं तव नारद ..
जन्मांतरसहस्रेषु नादत्तमुपतिष्ठते .. 7 ..
तस्मादन्नप्रदानेन सर्वे हृष्यंति जन्तवः ..
देवाश्च स्पृहयंत्येनमन्नदानप्रदायिनम् .. 8 ..
आज्यं देयं च पात्रेषु श्रद्धया वज्रमिश्रितम् ..
वज्रदानकरो मर्त्यश्चातुर्मास्ये न मानवः .. 9 ..
5.234.m:
Constantly giving food and water, giving a cow, / reciting the Vedas, and offering oblations into the fire during the Cāturmāsya yield great fruit.
If one desires the abode of Vaikuṇṭha, in union with Viṣṇu, / for the destruction of all sins one should be a giver of food during the Cāturmāsya.
Truly, truly indeed, O celestial seer Nārada, has this been spoken by me to you: / what has not been given does not attend one in a thousand other births.
Therefore, by the giving of food all living beings rejoice; / and the gods yearn for this giver of the gift of food.
And clarified butter mixed with diamonds should be given in vessels with faith; / a mortal who makes a gift of diamonds during the Cāturmāsya is no ordinary human.

5.234.s:
bhojanaṃ guruviprāṇāṃ ghṛtadānaṃ ca satkriyā ..
etāni yasya tiṣṭhanti cāturmāsye na mānavaḥ .. 6.235.10 ..
5.234.d:
भोजनं गुरुविप्राणां घृतदानं च सत्क्रिया ..
एतानि यस्य तिष्ठन्ति चातुर्मास्ये न मानवः .. 6.235.10 ..
5.234.m: Feeding venerable brahmins, giving ghee, and hospitality— / he in whom these abide during the Cāturmāsya is no ordinary human.

5.234.s:
saddharmaḥ satkathā caiva satsevā darśanaṃ satām ..
viṣṣupūjā ratirdāne cāturmāsyeṣu durlabhāḥ .. 11 ..
5.234.d:
सद्धर्मः सत्कथा चैव सत्सेवा दर्शनं सताम् ..
विष्षुपूजा रतिर्दाने चातुर्मास्येषु दुर्लभाः .. 11 ..
5.234.m: True dharma, sacred discourse, service to the virtuous, the darśana of the virtuous, / worship of Viṣṇu, and delight in giving are hard to obtain during the Cāturmāsyas.

5.234.s:
pitṝnuddiśya yo martyaścāturmāsye'nnado bhavet ..
sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā pitṛlokamavāmuyāt .. 12 ..
5.234.d:
पितॄनुद्दिश्य यो मर्त्यश्चातुर्मास्येऽन्नदो भवेत् ..
सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा पितृलोकमवामुयात् .. 12 ..
5.234.m: That mortal who becomes a giver of food during the Cāturmāsya for the sake of the ancestors, / his soul purified of all sins, would attain the realm of the ancestors.

5.234.s:
devāḥ sarve'nnadānena tṛptā yacchanti vāṃchitam ..
pipīlikā'pi yadgehādbhakṣyamādāya gacchati .. 13 ..
5.234.d:
देवाः सर्वेऽन्नदानेन तृप्ता यच्छन्ति वांछितम् ..
पिपीलिकाऽपि यद्गेहाद्भक्ष्यमादाय गच्छति .. 13 ..
5.234.m: All the gods, satisfied by the gift of food, bestow what is desired; / even an ant goes bearing food from his house.

5.234.s:
rātrau divā'niṣiddhānno hyannadānamanuttamam ..
harau supte hi pāpaghnaṃ vārya mapi śatruṣu .. 14 ..
5.234.d:
रात्रौ दिवाऽनिषिद्धान्नो ह्यन्नदानमनुत्तमम् ..
हरौ सुप्ते हि पापघ्नं वार्य मपि शत्रुषु .. 14 ..
5.234.m: Unforbidden food by night or day: the gift of food is unsurpassed; / while Hari is asleep, it destroys sins, even when offered to enemies.

5.234.s:
cāturmāsye dugdhadānaṃ dadhi takraṃ mahāphalam ..
janmakāle yena baddhaḥ piṃḍastaddānamuttamam .. 15 ..
5.234.d:
चातुर्मास्ये दुग्धदानं दधि तक्रं महाफलम् ..
जन्मकाले येन बद्धः पिंडस्तद्दानमुत्तमम् .. 15 ..
5.234.m: During the Cāturmāsya, the giving of milk, curds, and buttermilk yields great fruit; / that gift is supreme by which the bodily mass was formed at the time of birth.

5.234.s:
śākapradātā narakaṃ yamalokaṃ na paśyati ..
vastradaḥ somalokaṃ ca vasedābhūtasaṃplavam .. 16 ..
5.234.d:
शाकप्रदाता नरकं यमलोकं न पश्यति ..
वस्त्रदः सोमलोकं च वसेदाभूतसंप्लवम् .. 16 ..
5.234.m: A giver of vegetables does not see hell or the world of Yama; / a giver of garments would dwell in the world of Soma until the dissolution of beings.

5.234.s:
supte deve yathāśakti hyanyāsu pratimāsu ca ..
puṣpavastrapradānena santānaṃ naiva hīyate .. 17 ..
5.234.d:
सुप्ते देवे यथाशक्ति ह्यन्यासु प्रतिमासु च ..
पुष्पवस्त्रप्रदानेन सन्तानं नैव हीयते .. 17 ..
5.234.m: While the God is asleep, according to one's capacity, even to other icons, / by offering flowers and garments, lineage never declines.

5.234.s:
candanāgurudhūpaṃ ca cāturmāsye prayacchati ..
putrapautrasamāyukto viṣṇurūpī bhavennaraḥ ..18 ..
5.234.d:
चन्दनागुरुधूपं च चातुर्मास्ये प्रयच्छति ..
पुत्रपौत्रसमायुक्तो विष्णुरूपी भवेन्नरः ..18 ..
5.234.m: He who gives sandalwood and aloewood incense during the Cāturmāsya, / endowed with sons and grandsons, becomes one possessing the form of Viṣṇu.

5.234.s:
supte deve jagannāthe phaladānaṃ praya cchati ..
viprāya vedaviduṣe yamalokaṃ na paśyati .. 19 ..
5.234.d:
सुप्ते देवे जगन्नाथे फलदानं प्रय च्छति ..
विप्राय वेदविदुषे यमलोकं न पश्यति .. 19 ..
5.234.m: While the God, the Lord of the World, is asleep, whoever gives a gift of fruit / to a brahmin who knows the Vedas, does not see the world of Yama.

5.234.s:
vidyādānaṃ ca godānaṃ bhūmidānaṃ prayacchati ..
viṣṇuprītyarthameveha sa tārayati pūrvajān .. 6.235.20 ..
5.234.d:
विद्यादानं च गोदानं भूमिदानं प्रयच्छति ..
विष्णुप्रीत्यर्थमेवेह स तारयति पूर्वजान् .. 6.235.20 ..
5.234.m: Whoever gives the gift of knowledge, the gift of a cow, and the gift of land / solely for the pleasure of Viṣṇu, delivers his ancestors here.

5.234.s:
guḍasaiṃdhavatailādimadhutiktatilānnadaḥ ..
devatāyāssamuddiśya tāsāṃ lokaṃ prayāti hi .. 21 ..
5.234.d:
गुडसैंधवतैलादिमधुतिक्ततिलान्नदः ..
देवतायास्समुद्दिश्य तासां लोकं प्रयाति हि .. 21 ..
5.234.m: One who gives jaggery, rock salt, oil and the like, honey, bitter herbs, and sesame food / dedicated to a deity, departs indeed to their realm.

5.234.s:
cāturmāsye tilāndattvā na bhūyaḥ stanapo bhavet ..
yavapradātā vasate vāsavaṃ lokamakṣayam .. 22 ..
5.234.d:
चातुर्मास्ये तिलान्दत्त्वा न भूयः स्तनपो भवेत् ..
यवप्रदाता वसते वासवं लोकमक्षयम् .. 22 ..
5.234.m: Having given sesame seeds during the Cāturmāsya, one does not drink from a breast again; / a giver of barley dwells in the imperishable realm of Indra.

5.234.s:
hūyeta havyaṃ vahnau ca dānaṃ dadyāddvijātaye ..
gāvaḥ supūjitāḥ kāryāścāturmāsye viśeṣataḥ .. 23 ..
5.234.d:
हूयेत हव्यं वह्नौ च दानं दद्याद्द्विजातये ..
गावः सुपूजिताः कार्याश्चातुर्मास्ये विशेषतः .. 23 ..
5.234.m: Sacrificial food should be offered into the fire, and gifts should be given to the twice-born; / cows should be honored well, especially during the Cāturmāsya.

5.234.s:
yatkiṃcitsukṛtaṃ karma janmāvadhi susaṃcitam ..
cāturmāsye gate pātre vimukhe yanna dīyate .. 24 ..
5.234.d:
यत्किंचित्सुकृतं कर्म जन्मावधि सुसंचितम् ..
चातुर्मास्ये गते पात्रे विमुखे यन्न दीयते .. 24 ..
5.234.m: Whatever virtuous deed was well-accumulated since birth— / if, during the Cāturmāsya, when a worthy recipient departs turned away, it is not given,

5.234.s:
praṇaśyati kṣaṇādeva vacanā dyastu pracyutaḥ ..
divasedivase tasya varddhate ca pratiśrutam .. 25 ..
5.234.d:
प्रणश्यति क्षणादेव वचना द्यस्तु प्रच्युतः ..
दिवसेदिवसे तस्य वर्द्धते च प्रतिश्रुतम् .. 25 ..
5.234.m: it perishes in an instant; for whoever falls away from his word, / what was promised increases for him day by day.

5.234.s:
tasmānnaiva pratiśrāvyaṃ svalpamapyāśu dīyate ..
tāvadvivarddhate dānaṃ yāvattanna prayacchati .. 26 ..
5.234.d:
तस्मान्नैव प्रतिश्राव्यं स्वल्पमप्याशु दीयते ..
तावद्विवर्द्धते दानं यावत्तन्न प्रयच्छति .. 26 ..
5.234.m: Therefore one should not make a promise [unless] even a small thing is promptly given; / the obligation to give increases as long as one does not give it.

5.234.s:
yo mohānmanujo loke yāvatkoṭiguṇaṃ bhavet ..
tato daśaguṇā vṛddhiścāturmāsye pradātari .. 27 ..
5.234.d:
यो मोहान्मनुजो लोके यावत्कोटिगुणं भवेत् ..
ततो दशगुणा वृद्धिश्चातुर्मास्ये प्रदातरि .. 27 ..
5.234.m: That person who out of delusion in the world [fails to give], it becomes tenfold a crore of times; / then tenfold is the increase for the giver during the Cāturmāsya.

5.234.s:
narake patanaṃ tasya yāva diṃdrāścaturdaśa ..
atastu sarvadā deyaṃ narairyattu pratiśrutam .. 28 ..
5.234.d:
नरके पतनं तस्य याव दिंद्राश्चतुर्दश ..
अतस्तु सर्वदा देयं नरैर्यत्तु प्रतिश्रुतम् .. 28 ..
5.234.m: His fall into hell lasts as long as fourteen Indras reign; / therefore, whatever has been promised should always be given by men.

5.234.s:
anyasmai na pradātavyaṃ pradattaṃ naiva hārayet .
cāturmāsyeṣu yaḥ śayyāṃ dvijāgryāya prayacchati .. 29 ..
5.234.d:
अन्यस्मै न प्रदातव्यं प्रदत्तं नैव हारयेत् .
चातुर्मास्येषु यः शय्यां द्विजाग्र्याय प्रयच्छति .. 29 ..
5.234.m: It should not be given to another; what has been promised one must not forfeit. / During the Cāturmāsyas, he who gives a bed to an eminent twice-born,

5.234.s:
vedoktena vidhānena na sa yāti yamālayam ..
āsanaṃ vāripātraṃ ca bhājanaṃ tāmrabhājanam .. 6.235.30 ..
5.234.d:
वेदोक्तेन विधानेन न स याति यमालयम् ..
आसनं वारिपात्रं च भाजनं ताम्रभाजनम् .. 6.235.30 ..
5.234.m: According to the rite prescribed in the Vedas, he does not go to the abode of Yama. / A seat, a water vessel, and a utensil—a copper vessel—

5.234.s:
cāturmāsye prayatnena deyaṃ vittānusārataḥ ..
sarvadānāni viprebhyo dadatsupte jagadgurau .. 31 ..
5.234.d:
चातुर्मास्ये प्रयत्नेन देयं वित्तानुसारतः ..
सर्वदानानि विप्रेभ्यो ददत्सुप्ते जगद्गुरौ .. 31 ..
5.234.m: Should be given with effort during the Cāturmāsya according to one's wealth. / Giving all kinds of gifts to brahmins while the Teacher of the World is asleep,

5.234.s:
ātmānaṃ pūrvajaiḥ sārddhaṃ sa mocayati pātakāt ..
gaurbhūśca tilapātraṃ ca dīpadānamanuttamam .. 32 ..
5.234.d:
आत्मानं पूर्वजैः सार्द्धं स मोचयति पातकात् ..
गौर्भूश्च तिलपात्रं च दीपदानमनुत्तमम् .. 32 ..
5.234.m: He frees himself along with his ancestors from sin. / A cow, land, a vessel of sesame, and the supreme gift of a lamp:

5.234.s: dadadvijātaye mukto jāyate sa ṛṇatrayāt .. 33 ..
5.234.d: ददद्विजातये मुक्तो जायते स ऋणत्रयात् .. 33 ..
5.234.m: Giving [these] to a twice-born, he becomes released from the three debts.

5.234.s:
sa viśvakartā bhuvaneṣu goptā sa yajñabhuksarvaphalapradaśca ..
dānāni vastuṣvadhidaivataṃ ca yasminsamuddiśya dadāti muktaḥ .. 34 ..
5.234.d:
स विश्वकर्ता भुवनेषु गोप्ता स यज्ञभुक्सर्वफलप्रदश्च ..
दानानि वस्तुष्वधिदैवतं च यस्मिन्समुद्दिश्य ददाति मुक्तः .. 34 ..
5.234.m: He is the creator of the universe, the protector among the worlds; he is the enjoyer of sacrifice and the bestower of all fruits. / In whom [abides] the presiding deity over gifts and objects, addressing him, [the giver], liberated, offers [them].

5.234.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvara kṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne cāturmāsyamāhātmye brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsyadānamahimavarṇanaṃnāma pañcatriṃśaduttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. .. 235 ..
5.234.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वर क्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्यदानमहिमवर्णनंनाम पञ्चत्रिंशदुत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः .. .. 235 ..
5.234.m: Thus ends the two hundred and thirty-fifth chapter, titled 'Description of the Glory of Gifts during Cāturmāsya,' in the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada, in the Glory of Cāturmāsya, in the episode of Him Who Sleeps upon Śeṣa, in the Glory of the sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the sixth Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses] of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa.

5.235.s:
.. brahmovāca .. ..
iṣṭavastuprado viṣṇurlokaśceṣṭaruciḥ sadā ..
tasmātsarvaprayatnena cātumāsye tyajecca tat .. 1 ..
5.235.d:
.. ब्रह्मोवाच .. ..
इष्टवस्तुप्रदो विष्णुर्लोकश्चेष्टरुचिः सदा ..
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन चातुमास्ये त्यजेच्च तत् .. 1 ..
5.235.m: Brahmā said: / Viṣṇu is the giver of desired objects, and people always take pleasure in what is desired. / Therefore, with all effort, one should abandon that during Cāturmāsya.
For the pleasure of Nārāyaṇa, that very [gift] is obtained imperishably. / If a mortal gives it up with faith, he becomes the enjoyer of endless fruit.
From renouncing bronze vessels, one becomes a king on earth. / Eating from a palāśa leaf, one attains the state of Brahman.

5.235.s:
tāmrapātre na bhuñjīta kadācidvā gṛhī naraḥ ..
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa tāmrapātraṃ vivarjayet .. 4 ..
5.235.d:
ताम्रपात्रे न भुञ्जीत कदाचिद्वा गृही नरः ..
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण ताम्रपात्रं विवर्जयेत् .. 4 ..
5.235.m: A householder should never eat from a copper vessel. / Especially during Cāturmāsya, he should avoid a copper vessel.

5.235.s:
arkapatreṣu bhuñjāno'nupamaṃ labhate phalam ..
vaṭapatreṣu bhoktavyaṃ cāturmāsye viśeṣataḥ .. 5 ..
5.235.d:
अर्कपत्रेषु भुञ्जानोऽनुपमं लभते फलम् ..
वटपत्रेषु भोक्तव्यं चातुर्मास्ये विशेषतः .. 5 ..
5.235.m: Eating on arka leaves, one attains incomparable fruit. / One should eat on banyan leaves, especially during Cāturmāsya.

5.235.s:
aśvatthapatrasaṃbhogaḥ kāryo budhajanaiḥ sadā ..
ekānnabhojī rājā syātsakalaṃ bhūmimaṇḍale .. 6 ..
5.235.d:
अश्वत्थपत्रसंभोगः कार्यो बुधजनैः सदा ..
एकान्नभोजी राजा स्यात्सकलं भूमिमण्डले .. 6 ..
5.235.m: The use of aśvattha leaves should always be practiced by wise people. / One who eats once a day becomes a king over the entire circle of the earth.

5.235.s:
tathā ca lavaṇatyāgātsubhago jāyate naraḥ ..
godhūmānnaparityāgājjāyate janavalabhaḥ .. 7 ..
5.235.d:
तथा च लवणत्यागात्सुभगो जायते नरः ..
गोधूमान्नपरित्यागाज्जायते जनवलभः .. 7 ..
5.235.m: Likewise, from giving up salt, a man becomes charming. / From renouncing food made of wheat, he becomes beloved by the people.
During Cāturmāsya, one who eats no vegetables attains a long life. / From renouncing flavours, one has great vitality; from renouncing honey, one has beautiful eyes.
From giving up mudga beans comes the death of enemies; from cowpeas, great wealth. / From renouncing polished rice, obtaining horses comes to pass during Cāturmāsya.

5.235.s:
phalatyāgādbahusutastailatyāgātsurūpitā ..
jñānī tuvarisaṃtyāgādbalaṃ vīryaṃ sadaiva hi .. 6.236.10 ..
5.235.d:
फलत्यागाद्बहुसुतस्तैलत्यागात्सुरूपिता ..
ज्ञानी तुवरिसंत्यागाद्बलं वीर्यं सदैव हि .. 6.236.10 ..
5.235.m: From giving up fruit, many sons; from giving up oil, handsome appearance. / From renouncing pigeon peas, one becomes wise, possessing strength and vigour at all times.

5.235.s:
mārgamāṃsaparityāgānnarakaṃ na ca paśyati ..
śaukarasya pīratyāgādbrahmavāsamavāpnuyāt .. 11 ..
5.235.d:
मार्गमांसपरित्यागान्नरकं न च पश्यति ..
शौकरस्य पीरत्यागाद्ब्रह्मवासमवाप्नुयात् .. 11 ..
5.235.m: From renouncing venison, one does not see hell. / From giving up wild boar meat, one obtains residence in the world of Brahmā.

5.235.s:
jñānaṃ lāvakasantyāgādājyatyāge mahatsukham ..
āsavaṃ samparityajya muktistasya na durlabhā .. 12 ..
5.235.d:
ज्ञानं लावकसन्त्यागादाज्यत्यागे महत्सुखम् ..
आसवं सम्परित्यज्य मुक्तिस्तस्य न दुर्लभा .. 12 ..
5.235.m: Knowledge comes from renouncing quail meat; from giving up ghee, great happiness. / Having completely given up liquor, liberation is not hard for him to attain.

5.235.s:
sabalaḥ kanakatyāgādrūpyatyāgena mānuṣaḥ .. 69..
dadhidugdhaparityāgī goloke sukha bhāgbhavet .. 13
brahmā pāyasasaṃtyāgātkṣiprātyāgānmaheśvaraḥ ..
kandarpo'pūpasaṃtyāgānmodakatyājakaḥ sukhī .. 14 ..
gṛhāśramaparityāgī bāhyā śramaniṣevakaḥ ..
cāturmāsyaṃ hariprītyai na māturjaṭhare śiśuḥ .. 15 ..
nṛpo marīcasaṃtyāgācchuṇṭhītyāgena satkaviḥ ..
śarkarāyāḥ parityāgājjāyate rājapūjitaḥ .. 16 ..
guḍatyāgānmahābhūtistathā dāḍimavarjanāt ..
raktavastraparityāgājjāyate janavallabhaḥ .. 17 ..
paṭṭakūlaparityāgādakṣayyaṃ svarga māpnuyāt ..
māṣānnacaṇakānnasya tyāgānnaiva punarbhavaḥ .. 18 ..
kṛṣṇavastraṃ sadā tyājyaṃ cāturmāsye viśeṣataḥ ..
sūryasaṃdarśanācchuddhirnīlavastrasya darśanāt .. 19 ..
caṃdanasya parityāgādgāṃdharvaṃ lokamaśnute ..
karpūrasya parityāgādyāvajjīvaṃ mahādhanī .. 6.236.20 ..
5.235.d:
सबलः कनकत्यागाद्रूप्यत्यागेन मानुषः .. 69..
दधिदुग्धपरित्यागी गोलोके सुख भाग्भवेत् .. 13
ब्रह्मा पायससंत्यागात्क्षिप्रात्यागान्महेश्वरः ..
कन्दर्पोऽपूपसंत्यागान्मोदकत्याजकः सुखी .. 14 ..
गृहाश्रमपरित्यागी बाह्या श्रमनिषेवकः ..
चातुर्मास्यं हरिप्रीत्यै न मातुर्जठरे शिशुः .. 15 ..
नृपो मरीचसंत्यागाच्छुण्ठीत्यागेन सत्कविः ..
शर्करायाः परित्यागाज्जायते राजपूजितः .. 16 ..
गुडत्यागान्महाभूतिस्तथा दाडिमवर्जनात् ..
रक्तवस्त्रपरित्यागाज्जायते जनवल्लभः .. 17 ..
पट्टकूलपरित्यागादक्षय्यं स्वर्ग माप्नुयात् ..
माषान्नचणकान्नस्य त्यागान्नैव पुनर्भवः .. 18 ..
कृष्णवस्त्रं सदा त्याज्यं चातुर्मास्ये विशेषतः ..
सूर्यसंदर्शनाच्छुद्धिर्नीलवस्त्रस्य दर्शनात् .. 19 ..
चंदनस्य परित्यागाद्गांधर्वं लोकमश्नुते ..
कर्पूरस्य परित्यागाद्यावज्जीवं महाधनी .. 6.236.20 ..
5.235.m:
A man becomes powerful by giving up gold, and by giving up silver.
One who completely gives up curd and milk becomes an enjoyer of happiness in Goloka.
One becomes Brahmā from giving up rice pudding, and Maheśvara from giving up thin gruel; / one becomes Kāmadeva from giving up cakes, and happy from giving up modakas.
One who gives up the householder's stage of life and observes an outer hermitage / during Cāturmāsya for the pleasure of Hari, does not become an infant in a mother's womb.
A king comes from giving up black pepper; from giving up dry ginger, a good poet; / from giving up sugar, one becomes honoured by kings.
From giving up jaggery, great prosperity; likewise from avoiding pomegranate; / from giving up red cloth, one becomes beloved by the people.
From giving up silk cloth, one attains imperishable heaven. / From giving up food made of black gram and chickpeas, there is no rebirth.
Black cloth should always be avoided, especially during Cāturmāsya. / Purification from sighting blue cloth comes from seeing the sun.
From renouncing sandalwood, one attains the realm of the Gandharvas. / From renouncing camphor, one becomes exceedingly wealthy as long as one lives.

5.235.s:
kusumbhasya parityāgānnaiva paśyedyamāla yam ..
keśarasya parityāgānmanuṣyo rājavallabhaḥ .. 21 ..
yakṣakardamasaṃtyāgādbrahmaloke mahīyate ..
jñānī puṣpaparityāgācchayyātyāge mahatsu kham.. 22 ..
bhāryāviyogaṃ nāpnoti cāturmāsye na saṃśayaḥ ..
alīkavādasaṃtyāgānmokṣadvāramapāvṛtam .. 23 ..
paramarmaprakāśaśca sadyaḥpāpasamā gamaḥ ..
cāturmāsye harau supte paranindāṃ vivarjayet .. 24 ..
paranindā mahāpāpaṃ paranindā mahābhayam ..
paranindā mahadduḥkhaṃ na tasyāṃ pātakaṃ param .. 25 ..
kevalaṃ nindane caiva tatpāpaṃ labhate guru ..
yathā śṛṇvāna eva syātpātakī na tataḥ paraḥ .. 26 ..
keśasaṃskārasaṃtyāgāttāpatrayavivarjitaḥ ..
nakharomadharo yastu harau supte viśeṣataḥ .. 27 ..
divasedivase tasya gaṃgāsnānaphalaṃ bhavet .. 25 ..
5.235.d:
कुसुम्भस्य परित्यागान्नैव पश्येद्यमाल यम् ..
केशरस्य परित्यागान्मनुष्यो राजवल्लभः .. 21 ..
यक्षकर्दमसंत्यागाद्ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ..
ज्ञानी पुष्पपरित्यागाच्छय्यात्यागे महत्सु खम्.. 22 ..
भार्यावियोगं नाप्नोति चातुर्मास्ये न संशयः ..
अलीकवादसंत्यागान्मोक्षद्वारमपावृतम् .. 23 ..
परमर्मप्रकाशश्च सद्यःपापसमा गमः ..
चातुर्मास्ये हरौ सुप्ते परनिन्दां विवर्जयेत् .. 24 ..
परनिन्दा महापापं परनिन्दा महाभयम् ..
परनिन्दा महद्दुःखं न तस्यां पातकं परम् .. 25 ..
केवलं निन्दने चैव तत्पापं लभते गुरु ..
यथा शृण्वान एव स्यात्पातकी न ततः परः .. 26 ..
केशसंस्कारसंत्यागात्तापत्रयविवर्जितः ..
नखरोमधरो यस्तु हरौ सुप्ते विशेषतः .. 27 ..
दिवसेदिवसे तस्य गंगास्नानफलं भवेत् .. 25 ..
5.235.m:
From giving up safflower, one will never see the abode of Yama. / From giving up saffron, a man becomes beloved of kings.
From renouncing yakṣakardama perfume, one is honoured in the world of Brahmā. / One becomes wise from giving up flowers; from giving up a bed, great happiness.
He does not suffer separation from his wife during Cāturmāsya, without doubt. / From renouncing falsehood, the door to liberation is opened wide.
Revealing the secrets of others brings an immediate accumulation of sin. / During Cāturmāsya, while Hari is asleep, one must avoid slandering others.
Slandering others is a great sin; slandering others is a great danger; / slandering others is a great sorrow; there is no higher sin than it.
Merely by slandering, one incurs that grave sin; / even one merely hearing it becomes a sinner—none is greater than that.
From renouncing the grooming of hair, one is freed from the threefold misery. / But he who keeps his nails and hair, especially while Hari is asleep,
Attains day by day the fruit of bathing in the Gaṅgā.

5.235.s:
sarvopāyairviṣṇureva prasādyo yogidhyeyaḥ pravaraiḥ sarvavarṇeḥ ..
viṣṇornāmnā mucyate ghorabandhāccāturmāsye smaryate'sau viśeṣāt .. 29 ..
5.235.d:
सर्वोपायैर्विष्णुरेव प्रसाद्यो योगिध्येयः प्रवरैः सर्ववर्णेः ..
विष्णोर्नाम्ना मुच्यते घोरबन्धाच्चातुर्मास्ये स्मर्यतेऽसौ विशेषात् .. 29 ..
5.235.m: By all means Viṣṇu alone must be propitiated, who is to be meditated upon by yogins, by the best of all castes; / by Viṣṇu's name one is freed from terrible bondage, and he is especially to be remembered in Cāturmāsya.

5.235.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitā yāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne cāturmāsyamāhātmye brahmanāradasaṃvāda iṣṭavastuparityāgamahimavarṇanaṃnāma ṣaṭtriṃśaduttaradvi śatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 236 ..
5.235.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहिता यां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये ब्रह्मनारदसंवाद इष्टवस्तुपरित्यागमहिमवर्णनंनाम षट्त्रिंशदुत्तरद्वि शततमोऽध्यायः .. 236 ..
5.235.m: Thus ends the two hundred and thirty-sixth chapter, titled 'Description of the Glory of Renouncing Desired Objects,' in the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada, in the Glory of Cāturmāsya, in the episode of Him Who Sleeps upon Śeṣa, in the Glory of the sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the sixth Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses] of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa.

5.236.s:
.. nārada uvāca .. ..
kadā vidhiniṣedhau ca kartavyau viṣṇusannidhau ..
yuṣmadvākyāmṛtaṃ pītvā tṛptirmama na vidyate .. 1 ..
5.236.d:
.. नारद उवाच .. ..
कदा विधिनिषेधौ च कर्तव्यौ विष्णुसन्निधौ ..
युष्मद्वाक्यामृतं पीत्वा तृप्तिर्मम न विद्यते .. 1 ..
5.236.m: Nārada said: / When should the injunctions and prohibitions be undertaken in the presence of Viṣṇu? / Having drunk the nectar of your speech, there is no satiety for me.

5.236.s:
.. brahmovāca .. ..
karkasaṃkrāṃtidivase viṣṇuṃ saṃpūjya bhaktitaḥ ..
phalairarghyaḥ pradātavyaḥ śastajaṃbūphalaiḥ śubhaiḥ .. 2 ..
5.236.d:
.. ब्रह्मोवाच .. ..
कर्कसंक्रांतिदिवसे विष्णुं संपूज्य भक्तितः ..
फलैरर्घ्यः प्रदातव्यः शस्तजंबूफलैः शुभैः .. 2 ..
5.236.m: Brahmā said: / On the day of the summer solstice, having worshipped Viṣṇu with devotion, / an arghya offering should be given with fruits, with auspicious, praised jambū fruits.

5.236.s:
jaṃbūdvīpasya saṃjñeyaṃ phalena ca vijāyate ..
mantreṇānena vipreṃdra śraddhādharmasusaṃyataiḥ .. 3 ..
5.236.d:
जंबूद्वीपस्य संज्ञेयं फलेन च विजायते ..
मन्त्रेणानेन विप्रेंद्र श्रद्धाधर्मसुसंयतैः .. 3 ..
5.236.m: This name of Jambūdvīpa arises from that fruit. / With this mantra, O best of brahmins, by those who are fully restrained in faith and duty:

5.236.s:
ṣaṇmāsābhyaṃtare mṛtyuryatra kvāpi bhavenmama ..
tanmayā vāsudevāya svayamātmā niveditaḥ .. 4 ..
5.236.d:
षण्मासाभ्यंतरे मृत्युर्यत्र क्वापि भवेन्मम ..
तन्मया वासुदेवाय स्वयमात्मा निवेदितः .. 4 ..
5.236.m: 'If death should come to me anywhere within six months, / then my self has been surrendered by me to Vāsudeva.'

5.236.s:
.. iti maṃtreṇārghyam .. ..
tato vidhiniṣedhau ca grāhyau bhaktyā hareḥ puraḥ ..
cāturmāsye samāyāte sarvalokamahāsukhe .. 5 ..
5.236.d:
.. इति मंत्रेणार्घ्यम् .. ..
ततो विधिनिषेधौ च ग्राह्यौ भक्त्या हरेः पुरः ..
चातुर्मास्ये समायाते सर्वलोकमहासुखे .. 5 ..
5.236.m: Thus the arghya [is offered] with the mantra. / Then the injunctions and prohibitions should be accepted with devotion before Hari, / when Cāturmāsya has arrived, bringing great joy to all the worlds.

5.236.s:
vidhirvedavidhiḥ kāryo niṣedho niyamo mataḥ ..
vidhiścaiva niṣedhaśca dvāvetau viṣṇureva hi .. 6 ..
5.236.d:
विधिर्वेदविधिः कार्यो निषेधो नियमो मतः ..
विधिश्चैव निषेधश्च द्वावेतौ विष्णुरेव हि .. 6 ..
5.236.m: The injunction to be performed is the Vedic injunction; prohibition is regarded as restraint. / Both the injunction and the prohibition are indeed Viṣṇu himself.

5.236.s:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena sevya eva janārdanaḥ ..
viṣṇoḥ kathā viṣṇupūjā dhyānaṃ viṣṇornatistathā . 7 ..
5.236.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन सेव्य एव जनार्दनः ..
विष्णोः कथा विष्णुपूजा ध्यानं विष्णोर्नतिस्तथा . 7 ..
5.236.m: Therefore, by every effort Janārdana is indeed to be served: / discourse on Viṣṇu, worship of Viṣṇu, meditation on Viṣṇu, and likewise bowing to Viṣṇu.

5.236.s:
sarvameva hariprītyā yaḥ karoti sa muktibhāk ..
varṇāśramavidhermūrtiḥ satyo viṣṇuḥ sanātanaḥ .. 8 ..
5.236.d:
सर्वमेव हरिप्रीत्या यः करोति स मुक्तिभाक् ..
वर्णाश्रमविधेर्मूर्तिः सत्यो विष्णुः सनातनः .. 8 ..
5.236.m: Whoever does everything out of love for Hari partakes of liberation; / eternal Viṣṇu is the truth, the embodiment of the ordinances of class and life-stage.

5.236.s:
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa janmakaṣṭādināśanam ..
harireva vratādgrāhyo vrataṃ dehena kārayet ..
deho'yaṃ tapasā śodhyaḥ supte deve taponidhau .. 29 ..
.. nārada uvāca .. ..
kiṃ vrataṃ kiṃ tapaḥ proktaṃ brahmanbrūhi savistaram ..
supte deve mayā kāryaṃ kṛtaṃ yacca mahāphalam .. 6.237.10 ..
.. brahmovāca .. ..
vrataṃ viṣṇuvrataṃ viddhi viṣṇubhaktisamanvitam ..
tapaśca dharmavartitvaṃ kṛcchrādikamathāpi vā .. 11 ..
śṛṇu vratasya māhātmyaṃ vakṣyāmi prathamaṃ tava ..
brahmacaryavrataṃ sāraṃ vratānāmuttamaṃ vratam .. 12 ..
brahmacaryaṃ tapaḥ sāraṃ brahmacaryaṃ mahatphalam ..
kriyāsu sakalāsveva brahmacaryaṃ vivarddhayet .. 13 ..
brahmacaryaprabhāveṇa tapa ugraṃ pravarttate ..
brahmacaryātparaṃ nāsti dharmasādhana muttamam.. 14 ..
5.236.d:
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण जन्मकष्टादिनाशनम् ..
हरिरेव व्रताद्ग्राह्यो व्रतं देहेन कारयेत् ..
देहोऽयं तपसा शोध्यः सुप्ते देवे तपोनिधौ .. 29 ..
.. नारद उवाच .. ..
किं व्रतं किं तपः प्रोक्तं ब्रह्मन्ब्रूहि सविस्तरम् ..
सुप्ते देवे मया कार्यं कृतं यच्च महाफलम् .. 6.237.10 ..
.. ब्रह्मोवाच .. ..
व्रतं विष्णुव्रतं विद्धि विष्णुभक्तिसमन्वितम् ..
तपश्च धर्मवर्तित्वं कृच्छ्रादिकमथापि वा .. 11 ..
शृणु व्रतस्य माहात्म्यं वक्ष्यामि प्रथमं तव ..
ब्रह्मचर्यव्रतं सारं व्रतानामुत्तमं व्रतम् .. 12 ..
ब्रह्मचर्यं तपः सारं ब्रह्मचर्यं महत्फलम् ..
क्रियासु सकलास्वेव ब्रह्मचर्यं विवर्द्धयेत् .. 13 ..
ब्रह्मचर्यप्रभावेण तप उग्रं प्रवर्त्तते ..
ब्रह्मचर्यात्परं नास्ति धर्मसाधन मुत्तमम्.. 14 ..
5.236.m:
Especially during the Cāturmāsya, the destruction of the miseries of birth and the like [occurs]; / Hari alone is to be attained through vows; one should perform the vow with one's body. / This body must be purified by austerity while the Lord, the treasure of austerity, is asleep.
Nārada said: / What vow, what austerity is prescribed, O Brahmā? Tell [me] in detail / what is to be done by me while the Lord is asleep, which yields great fruit when performed.
Brahmā said: / Know the vow to be Viṣṇu's vow, accompanied by devotion to Viṣṇu; / and austerity to be abiding in righteousness, or else [performing] penances such as the kṛcchra.
Listen, I shall first describe to you the greatness of the vow: / the vow of celibacy is the essence, the supreme vow among vows.
Celibacy is the essence of austerity; celibacy bears great fruit. / In all ritual actions indeed one should augment celibacy.
By the power of celibacy, fierce austerity proceeds. / There is no supreme means of righteousness higher than celibacy.

5.236.s:
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa supte deve guṇottaram ..
mahāvratamidaṃ loke tannibodha sadā dvija .. 15 ..
nārāyaṇamidaṃ karma yaḥ karoti na lipyate ..
śatatrayaṃ ṣaṣṭiyutaṃ dinamāhuśca vatsare .. 16 ..
tatra nārāyaṇo devaḥ pūjyate vratakāribhiḥ ..
satkriyāmamukīṃ deva kārayiṣyāmi niścayaḥ .. 17 ..
kurute tadvrataṃ prāhuḥ supte deve guṇottaram ..
vahnihomo viprabhaktiḥ śraddhā dharme matiḥ śubhā .. 18 ..
satsaṃgo viṣṇupūjā ca satyavādo dayā hṛdi..
ārjavaṃ madhurā vāṇī saccaritre sadā ratiḥ .. 19 ..
vedapāṭhastathā'steyamahiṃsā hrīḥ kṣamā damaḥ ..
nirlobhatā'krodhatā ca nirmoho'mamatā'ra tiḥ .. 20 ..
śrutikriyāparaṃ jñānaṃ kṛṣṇārpitamanogatiḥ ..
etāni yasya tiṣṭhaṃti vratāni brahmavittama .. 21 ..
jīvanmukto naraḥ prokto naiva lipya ti pātakaiḥ ..
vrataṃ kṛtaṃ sakṛdapi sadaiva hi mahāphalam .. 22 ..
5.236.d:
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण सुप्ते देवे गुणोत्तरम् ..
महाव्रतमिदं लोके तन्निबोध सदा द्विज .. 15 ..
नारायणमिदं कर्म यः करोति न लिप्यते ..
शतत्रयं षष्टियुतं दिनमाहुश्च वत्सरे .. 16 ..
तत्र नारायणो देवः पूज्यते व्रतकारिभिः ..
सत्क्रियाममुकीं देव कारयिष्यामि निश्चयः .. 17 ..
कुरुते तद्व्रतं प्राहुः सुप्ते देवे गुणोत्तरम् ..
वह्निहोमो विप्रभक्तिः श्रद्धा धर्मे मतिः शुभा .. 18 ..
सत्संगो विष्णुपूजा च सत्यवादो दया हृदि..
आर्जवं मधुरा वाणी सच्चरित्रे सदा रतिः .. 19 ..
वेदपाठस्तथाऽस्तेयमहिंसा ह्रीः क्षमा दमः ..
निर्लोभताऽक्रोधता च निर्मोहोऽममताऽर तिः .. 20 ..
श्रुतिक्रियापरं ज्ञानं कृष्णार्पितमनोगतिः ..
एतानि यस्य तिष्ठंति व्रतानि ब्रह्मवित्तम .. 21 ..
जीवन्मुक्तो नरः प्रोक्तो नैव लिप्य ति पातकैः ..
व्रतं कृतं सकृदपि सदैव हि महाफलम् .. 22 ..
5.236.m:
Especially during Cāturmāsya, while the Lord is asleep, it is superior in virtues; / always understand this great vow in the world, O twice-born!
Whoever performs this work dedicated to Nārāyaṇa is not tainted. / They speak of three hundred and sixty days in a year;
there the Lord Nārāyaṇa is worshipped by vow-observers: / 'O Lord, I shall perform such-and-such good deed'—[such is] the resolve.
They declare that vow which one undertakes while the Lord is asleep to be superior in virtue: / offering oblations in fire, devotion to brahmins, faith, an auspicious mind set on righteousness,
association with the good, worship of Viṣṇu, speaking the truth, compassion in the heart, / uprightness, sweet speech, and continuous delight in good conduct,
recitation of the Veda, non-stealing, non-violence, modesty, patience, self-restraint, / absence of greed, absence of anger, freedom from delusion, absence of possessiveness, and dispassion,
knowledge dedicated to the rites of scripture, the mind's course offered to Kṛṣṇa— / for whom these vows are established, O best of the knowers of the Brahman,
that man is called liberated while living; he is never tainted by sins. / A vow performed even once always bears great fruit.

5.236.s:
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa brahmacaryādisevanam ..
avratena gataṃ yeṣāṃ cāturmāsyaṃ sadā nṛṇām .. 23 ..
dharmasteṣāṃ vṛthā sadbhistattvajñaiḥ parikīrtitaḥ ..
sarveṣāmeva varṇānāṃ vratacaryā mahāphalam .. 24 ..
svalpāpi vihitā vatsa cāturmā sye sukhapradā ..
sarvatra dṛśyate viṣṇurvratasevāparairnṛbhiḥ .. 25 ..
cāturmāsye samāyāte pālayettatprayatnataḥ .. 26 ..
bhajasva viṣṇuṃ dvijavahnitīrthavedaprabhedamayamūrtimajaṃ virājam ..
yatprasādādbhavati mokṣamahātarusthastāpaṃ na yāsyati bhavārkasamudbhavaṃ tam .. 27 ..
5.236.d:
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण ब्रह्मचर्यादिसेवनम् ..
अव्रतेन गतं येषां चातुर्मास्यं सदा नृणाम् .. 23 ..
धर्मस्तेषां वृथा सद्भिस्तत्त्वज्ञैः परिकीर्तितः ..
सर्वेषामेव वर्णानां व्रतचर्या महाफलम् .. 24 ..
स्वल्पापि विहिता वत्स चातुर्मा स्ये सुखप्रदा ..
सर्वत्र दृश्यते विष्णुर्व्रतसेवापरैर्नृभिः .. 25 ..
चातुर्मास्ये समायाते पालयेत्तत्प्रयत्नतः .. 26 ..
भजस्व विष्णुं द्विजवह्नितीर्थवेदप्रभेदमयमूर्तिमजं विराजम् ..
यत्प्रसादाद्भवति मोक्षमहातरुस्थस्तापं न यास्यति भवार्कसमुद्भवं तम् .. 27 ..
5.236.m:
Especially during Cāturmāsya, the practice of celibacy and the like [is fruitful]. / For those men whose Cāturmāsya has passed without any vow,
their righteousness has been proclaimed in vain by the virtuous knowers of reality. / The practice of vows bears great fruit for all classes indeed.
Even a little [vow] observed in Cāturmāsya, my child, bestows happiness. / Viṣṇu is seen everywhere by men intent on the observance of vows.
When Cāturmāsya has arrived, one should maintain it with effort.
Worship Viṣṇu, whose form consists of the distinctions of brahmins, fire, sacred fords, and the Vedas, the unborn, the radiant, / by whose grace one stands on the great tree of liberation and will not experience the distress born of the sun of worldly existence.

5.236.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsyamāhātmye vratamahimavarṇanaṃnāma saptatriṃ śaduttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 237 ..
5.236.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये व्रतमहिमवर्णनंनाम सप्तत्रिं शदुत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः .. 237 ..
5.236.m: Thus ends the two hundred and thirty-seventh chapter, named 'Description of the Greatness of Vows in the Greatness of Cāturmāsya,' in the conversation between Brahmā and Nārada, in the account of the one who sleeps on Śeṣa, in the glorification of the sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] in the venerable Skanda Purāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

5.237.s:
.. brahmovāca .. ..
tapaḥ śṛṇuṣva vipreṃdra vistareṇa mahāmate ..
yasya śravaṇamātreṇa cāturmāsye', ghanāśanam .. 1 ..
5.237.d:
.. ब्रह्मोवाच .. ..
तपः शृणुष्व विप्रेंद्र विस्तरेण महामते ..
यस्य श्रवणमात्रेण चातुर्मास्ये', घनाशनम् .. 1 ..
5.237.m: Brahmā said: / Hear of austerity in detail, O foremost of brahmins, O highly intelligent one, / by the mere hearing of which sins are destroyed during Cāturmāsya.

5.237.s:
ṣoḍaśairupacāraiśca viṣṇoḥ pūjā sadā tapaḥ ..
tataḥ supte jagannāthe mahattapa udāhṛtam .. 2 ..
5.237.d:
षोडशैरुपचारैश्च विष्णोः पूजा सदा तपः ..
ततः सुप्ते जगन्नाथे महत्तप उदाहृतम् .. 2 ..
5.237.m: Worship of Viṣṇu with the sixteen articles of reverence is always austerity; / moreover, while the Lord of the world is asleep, it is declared to be great austerity.

5.237.s:
karaṇaṃ paṃcayajñānāṃ satataṃ tapa eva hi ..
tannivedya harau caiva cāturmāsye mahattapaḥ .. 3 ..
5.237.d:
करणं पंचयज्ञानां सततं तप एव हि ..
तन्निवेद्य हरौ चैव चातुर्मास्ये महत्तपः .. 3 ..
5.237.m: The continuous performance of the five great sacrifices is indeed austerity; / offering it to Hari, especially during Cāturmāsya, is great austerity.

5.237.s:
ṛtuyānaṃ gṛhasthasya tapa eva sadaiva hi ..
cāturmāsye hariprītyai tanniṣevyaṃ mahattapaḥ .. 4 ..
5.237.d:
ऋतुयानं गृहस्थस्य तप एव सदैव हि ..
चातुर्मास्ये हरिप्रीत्यै तन्निषेव्यं महत्तपः .. 4 ..
5.237.m: Approaching one's wife at the proper fertile period is always austerity for a householder; / observing it for the gratification of Hari during Cāturmāsya is great austerity.

5.237.s:
satyavādastapo nityaṃ prāṇināṃ bhuvi durlabham ..
supte devapatau kurvannanaṃtaphalabhāgbhavet .. 5 ..
5.237.d:
सत्यवादस्तपो नित्यं प्राणिनां भुवि दुर्लभम् ..
सुप्ते देवपतौ कुर्वन्ननंतफलभाग्भवेत् .. 5 ..
5.237.m: Speaking the truth is an enduring austerity difficult to obtain for living beings on earth; / performing it while the Lord of the gods is asleep, one partakes of endless fruit.

5.237.s:
ahiṃsādiguṇānāṃ ca pālanaṃ satataṃ tapaḥ ..
cāturmāsye tyaktavairaṃ mahattapa udāradhīḥ .. 6 ..
5.237.d:
अहिंसादिगुणानां च पालनं सततं तपः ..
चातुर्मास्ये त्यक्तवैरं महत्तप उदारधीः .. 6 ..
5.237.m: The constant maintenance of virtues such as non-violence is austerity; / abandoning enmity during Cāturmāsya, a person of noble intellect performs great austerity.

5.237.s:
tapa eva mahanmartyaḥ paṃcāyatanapūjanam ..
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa hariprītyā samācaret .. 7 .. ..
5.237.d:
तप एव महन्मर्त्यः पंचायतनपूजनम् ..
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण हरिप्रीत्या समाचरेत् .. 7 .. ..
5.237.m: Worship of the five deities is indeed a great austerity for a mortal; / one should perform it especially during Cāturmāsya for the love of Hari.

5.237.s:
.. nārada uvāca .. ..
paṃcāyatanasaṃjñeyaṃ kasyoktā sā kathaṃ bhavet ..
kathaṃ pūjā ca kartavyā vistareṇāśu tadvada .. 8 ..
5.237.d:
.. नारद उवाच .. ..
पंचायतनसंज्ञेयं कस्योक्ता सा कथं भवेत् ..
कथं पूजा च कर्तव्या विस्तरेणाशु तद्वद .. 8 ..
5.237.m: Nārada said: / What is meant by this term 'group of five deities'? How does it come to be? / And how should the worship be performed? Tell that quickly in detail.

5.237.s:
.. brahmovāca .. ..
prātarmadhyāhnapūjāyāṃ madhye pūjyo raviḥ sadā ..
rātrau madhye bhaveccaṃdrastadvarṇakusumaiḥ śubhaiḥ .. 9 ..
5.237.d:
.. ब्रह्मोवाच .. ..
प्रातर्मध्याह्नपूजायां मध्ये पूज्यो रविः सदा ..
रात्रौ मध्ये भवेच्चंद्रस्तद्वर्णकुसुमैः शुभैः .. 9 ..
5.237.m: Brahmā said: / In the morning and midday worship, the Sun is always to be worshipped in the centre; / at night the Moon should be in the centre, with auspicious flowers of matching color.

5.237.s:
vahnikoṇe tu heraṃbaṃ sarvavighnopaśāṃtaye ..
raktacaṃdana puṣpaiśca cāturmāsye viśeṣataḥ .. 6.238.10 ..
5.237.d:
वह्निकोणे तु हेरंबं सर्वविघ्नोपशांतये ..
रक्तचंदन पुष्पैश्च चातुर्मास्ये विशेषतः .. 6.238.10 ..
5.237.m: In the south-east corner [worship] Heramba for the pacification of all obstacles, / with red sandalwood and flowers, especially during Cāturmāsya.

5.237.s:
nairṛtaṃ dalamāsthāya bhagavānduṣṭadarpahā ..
gṛhasthasya sadā śatruvināśaṃ vidadhāti saḥ .. 11 ..
5.237.d:
नैरृतं दलमास्थाय भगवान्दुष्टदर्पहा ..
गृहस्थस्य सदा शत्रुविनाशं विदधाति सः .. 11 ..
5.237.m: Remaining upon the south-west petal, the Lord who destroys the pride of the wicked / continually brings about the destruction of the enemies of the householder.

5.237.s:
nairṛtyakoṇagaṃ viṣṇuṃ pūjayetsarvadā budhaḥ ..
sugandhacaṃdanaiḥ puṣpairnaivedyaiścātiśobhanaiḥ .. 12 ..
5.237.d:
नैरृत्यकोणगं विष्णुं पूजयेत्सर्वदा बुधः ..
सुगन्धचंदनैः पुष्पैर्नैवेद्यैश्चातिशोभनैः .. 12 ..
5.237.m: The wise man should always worship Viṣṇu placed in the south-west corner / with fragrant sandalwood, flowers, and exceedingly beautiful food offerings.

5.237.s:
gotrajā vāyukoṇe tu pūjanīyā sadā budhaiḥ ..
putrapautrapravṛddhyarthaṃ sumanobhirmanoharaiḥ .. 13 ..
5.237.d:
गोत्रजा वायुकोणे तु पूजनीया सदा बुधैः ..
पुत्रपौत्रप्रवृद्ध्यर्थं सुमनोभिर्मनोहरैः .. 13 ..
5.237.m: In the north-west corner, the family deity should always be worshipped by the wise / with charming blossoms for the increase of sons and grandsons.

5.237.s:
aiśāne bhagavānrudraḥ śvetapuṣpaiḥ sadā'rcitaḥ ..
apamṛtyuvināśāya sarvadoṣāpanuttaye .. 14 ..
5.237.d:
ऐशाने भगवान्रुद्रः श्वेतपुष्पैः सदाऽर्चितः ..
अपमृत्युविनाशाय सर्वदोषापनुत्तये .. 14 ..
5.237.m: In the north-east, the Lord Rudra is always worshipped with white flowers / for the destruction of untimely death and for the removal of all defects.

5.237.s:
jāgarti mahimā yasya brahmādyairnaiva likhyate ..
paṃcāyatanametaddhi pūjyate gṛhamedhibhiḥ .. 15 ..
5.237.d:
जागर्ति महिमा यस्य ब्रह्माद्यैर्नैव लिख्यते ..
पंचायतनमेतद्धि पूज्यते गृहमेधिभिः .. 15 ..
5.237.m: His greatness is awake, which cannot be inscribed even by Brahmā and the others; / this fivefold sanctuary is indeed worshipped by householders.

5.237.s:
tapa etatsadā kāryaṃ cāturmāsye mahāphalam ..
parvakāleṣu sarveṣu dānaṃ deyaṃ tapaḥ sadā ..
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa tadanaṃtaṃ prajāyate .. 16 ..
5.237.d:
तप एतत्सदा कार्यं चातुर्मास्ये महाफलम् ..
पर्वकालेषु सर्वेषु दानं देयं तपः सदा ..
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण तदनंतं प्रजायते .. 16 ..
5.237.m: This austerity is always to be performed; it bears great fruit in Cāturmāsya. / Giving gifts on all festival occasions is always an austerity; / especially during Cāturmāsya, that becomes infinite.

5.237.s:
śaucaṃ tu dvividhaṃ grāhyaṃ bāhyamābhyaṃtaraṃ sadā ..
jalaśaucaṃ tathā bāhyaṃ śraddhayā cāṃtaraṃ bhavet .. .. 17 ..
5.237.d:
शौचं तु द्विविधं ग्राह्यं बाह्यमाभ्यंतरं सदा ..
जलशौचं तथा बाह्यं श्रद्धया चांतरं भवेत् .. .. 17 ..
5.237.m: Purity is always to be understood as twofold: external and internal; / external is cleansing with water, and internal is through faith.

5.237.s:
idriyāṇāṃ grahaḥ kāryastapaso lakṣaṇaṃ param ..
nivṛttyeṃdriyalaulyaṃ ca cāturmāsye mahattapaḥ .. 18 ..
5.237.d:
इद्रियाणां ग्रहः कार्यस्तपसो लक्षणं परम् ..
निवृत्त्येंद्रियलौल्यं च चातुर्मास्ये महत्तपः .. 18 ..
5.237.m: Restraint of the senses should be maintained; it is the supreme characteristic of austerity. / The cessation of sensual desire during Cāturmāsya is great austerity.

5.237.s:
indriyāśvānsanniyamya satataṃ sukhamedhate ..
narake pātyate prāṇaistairevotpathagāmibhiḥ .. 19 ..
5.237.d:
इन्द्रियाश्वान्सन्नियम्य सततं सुखमेधते ..
नरके पात्यते प्राणैस्तैरेवोत्पथगामिभिः .. 19 ..
5.237.m: Having thoroughly curbed the horses of the senses, one continually prospers in happiness; / one is cast into hell by those very [senses] when they stray onto wrong paths.

5.237.s:
mamatārūpiṇīṃ grāhīṃ duṣṭāṃ nirbhartsya nigrahet ..
tapa eva sadā puṃsāṃ cāturmāsye'dhigauravam .. 6.238.20 ..
5.237.d:
ममतारूपिणीं ग्राहीं दुष्टां निर्भर्त्स्य निग्रहेत् ..
तप एव सदा पुंसां चातुर्मास्येऽधिगौरवम् .. 6.238.20 ..
5.237.m: Having rebuked the wicked grasping [female demon] in the form of possessiveness, he should subdue her. / For men, austerity is always of the highest importance during the Cāturmāsya.

5.237.s:
kāma eṣa mahāśatrustamekaṃ nirjayeddṛḍham ..
jitakāmā mahātmānastairjitaṃ nikhilaṃ jagat .. 21 ..
5.237.d:
काम एष महाशत्रुस्तमेकं निर्जयेद्दृढम् ..
जितकामा महात्मानस्तैर्जितं निखिलं जगत् .. 21 ..
5.237.m: This desire is a great enemy; one must firmly conquer it alone. / Those who have conquered desire are great souls; by them the entire world is conquered.

5.237.s:
etacca tapaso mūlaṃ tapaso mūlameva tat ..
sarvadā kāmavijayaḥ saṃkalpavijayastathā .. 22 ..
5.237.d:
एतच्च तपसो मूलं तपसो मूलमेव तत् ..
सर्वदा कामविजयः संकल्पविजयस्तथा .. 22 ..
5.237.m: And this is the root of austerity, indeed that very root of austerity: / constant victory over desire, as well as victory over mental resolve.

5.237.s:
tadeva hi paraṃ jñānaṃ kāmo yena prajāyate ..
mahattapastadevāhuścātumāsye phalottamam ..23..
5.237.d:
तदेव हि परं ज्ञानं कामो येन प्रजायते ..
महत्तपस्तदेवाहुश्चातुमास्ये फलोत्तमम् ..23..
5.237.m: For that indeed is supreme knowledge, by which desire is [overcome]; / they declare that very thing to be great austerity, yielding the highest fruit in the Cāturmāsya.

5.237.s:
lobhaḥ sadā parityājyaḥ pāpaṃ lobhe samāsthitam ..
tapastasyaiva vijayaścāturmāsye viśeṣataḥ .. 24 ..
5.237.d:
लोभः सदा परित्याज्यः पापं लोभे समास्थितम् ..
तपस्तस्यैव विजयश्चातुर्मास्ये विशेषतः .. 24 ..
5.237.m: Greed must always be abandoned; sin is seated in greed. / Austerity is indeed the conquest of it, especially in the Cāturmāsya.

5.237.s:
mohaḥ sadā'vivekaśca varjanīyaḥ prayatnataḥ ..
tena tyakto naro jñānī na jñānī mohasaṃśrayāta ..25..
5.237.d:
मोहः सदाऽविवेकश्च वर्जनीयः प्रयत्नतः ..
तेन त्यक्तो नरो ज्ञानी न ज्ञानी मोहसंश्रयात ..25..
5.237.m: Delusion and lack of discernment must always be avoided with effort. / A man freed from them is wise; one who relies on delusion is not wise.

5.237.s:
mada eva manuṣyāṇāṃ śarīrastho mahāripuḥ ..
sadā sa eva nigrāhyaḥ supte deve viśeṣataḥ ..26..
5.237.d:
मद एव मनुष्याणां शरीरस्थो महारिपुः ..
सदा स एव निग्राह्यः सुप्ते देवे विशेषतः ..26..
5.237.m: Arrogance alone is the great enemy residing in the body of men. / It must always be restrained, especially while the God is asleep.

5.237.s:
mānaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu vasatyeva bhayāvahaḥ ..
kṣamayā taṃ vinirjitya cāturmāsye guṇādhikaḥ..27..
5.237.d:
मानः सर्वेषु भूतेषु वसत्येव भयावहः ..
क्षमया तं विनिर्जित्य चातुर्मास्ये गुणाधिकः..27..
5.237.m: Pride indeed dwells in all living beings, causing fear. / Having conquered it through forbearance, one excels in virtue in the Cāturmāsya.

5.237.s:
mātsaryaṃ nirjayetprājño mahāpātakakāraṇam ..
cāturmāsye jitaṃ tena trailokyamamaraiḥ saha ..28..
5.237.d:
मात्सर्यं निर्जयेत्प्राज्ञो महापातककारणम् ..
चातुर्मास्ये जितं तेन त्रैलोक्यममरैः सह ..28..
5.237.m: A wise man should conquer envy, which is the cause of great sins. / During the Cāturmāsya, the three worlds together with the immortals are conquered by him.

5.237.s:
ahaṃkārasamākrāṃtā munayo vijiteṃdriyāḥ ..
dharmamārgaṃ parityajya kurvatyunmārgajāṃ kriyām ..29..
ahaṃkāraṃ parityajya satataṃ sukhamāpnuyāt ..
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa tasya tyāge mahāphalam ..6.238.3...
5.237.d:
अहंकारसमाक्रांता मुनयो विजितेंद्रियाः ..
धर्ममार्गं परित्यज्य कुर्वत्युन्मार्गजां क्रियाम् ..29..
अहंकारं परित्यज्य सततं सुखमाप्नुयात् ..
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण तस्य त्यागे महाफलम् ..6.238.3...
5.237.m:
Overpowered by egoism, even sages who have conquered their senses, / abandoning the path of righteousness, perform actions born of the wrong path.
Having abandoned egoism, one will obtain constant happiness. / Especially in the Cāturmāsya, there is great fruit in abandoning it.

5.237.s:
etaddhi tapaso mūlaṃ yadetanmanasastyajet ..
tyakteṣveteṣu sarveṣu para brahmamayo bhavet .. 31 ..
5.237.d:
एतद्धि तपसो मूलं यदेतन्मनसस्त्यजेत् ..
त्यक्तेष्वेतेषु सर्वेषु पर ब्रह्ममयो भवेत् .. 31 ..
5.237.m: For this is the root of austerity, that one should cast this out from the mind. / When all these are abandoned, one becomes composed of the supreme Brahman.

5.237.s:
prathamaṃ kāyaśuddhyarthaṃ prājāpatyaṃ samācaret ..
śayane devadevasya viśeṣeṇa mahattapaḥ .. 32 ..
5.237.d:
प्रथमं कायशुद्ध्यर्थं प्राजापत्यं समाचरेत् ..
शयने देवदेवस्य विशेषेण महत्तपः .. 32 ..
5.237.m: First, for the purification of the body, one should perform the Prājāpatya penance; / it is great austerity, especially during the sleep of the God of gods.

5.237.s:
harestu śayane nityamekāṃtaramu poṣaṇam ..
yaḥ karoti naro bhaktyā na sa gacchedyamālayam .. 33 ..
5.237.d:
हरेस्तु शयने नित्यमेकांतरमु पोषणम् ..
यः करोति नरो भक्त्या न स गच्छेद्यमालयम् .. 33 ..
5.237.m: The man who, with devotion, regularly undertakes fasting on alternate days / during Hari's sleep, will not go to the abode of Yama.

5.237.s:
harisvāpe naro nityamekabhaktaṃ samācaret ..
divasedivase tasya dvādaśāhaphalaṃ labhet .. 34 ..
5.237.d:
हरिस्वापे नरो नित्यमेकभक्तं समाचरेत् ..
दिवसेदिवसे तस्य द्वादशाहफलं लभेत् .. 34 ..
5.237.m: During Hari's sleep, a man should constantly observe [eating] a single meal; / day after day he obtains the fruit of a twelve-day sacrifice.

5.237.s:
cāturmāsye naro yastu śākāhāraparo yadi ..
puṇyaṃ kratusahasrāṇāṃ jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 35 ..
5.237.d:
चातुर्मास्ये नरो यस्तु शाकाहारपरो यदि ..
पुण्यं क्रतुसहस्राणां जायते नात्र संशयः .. 35 ..
5.237.m: If a man devotes himself to eating only vegetables during the Cāturmāsya, / the merit of a thousand sacrifices is generated; there is no doubt about this.

5.237.s:
cāturmāsye naro nityaṃ cāṃdrāya ṇavrataṃ caret ..
ekaikamāse tatpuṇyaṃ varṇituṃ naiva śakyate .. 36 ..
5.237.d:
चातुर्मास्ये नरो नित्यं चांद्राय णव्रतं चरेत् ..
एकैकमासे तत्पुण्यं वर्णितुं नैव शक्यते .. 36 ..
5.237.m: If a man constantly observes the Cāndrāyaṇa vow during the Cāturmāsya, / the merit of each single month cannot possibly be described.

5.237.s:
supte deve ca pārākaṃ yaḥ karoti viśuddhadhīḥ ..
nārī vā śraddhayā yuktā śatajanmāgha nāśanam .. 37 ..
5.237.d:
सुप्ते देवे च पाराकं यः करोति विशुद्धधीः ..
नारी वा श्रद्धया युक्ता शतजन्माघ नाशनम् .. 37 ..
5.237.m: And while the God is asleep, whoever of purified intellect performs the Pārāka penance, / or a woman endowed with faith, it destroys the sins of a hundred births.

5.237.s:
kṛcchrasevī bhavedyastu supte deve janārdane ..
pāparāśiṃ vinirdhūya vaikuṇṭhe gaṇatāṃ vrajet .. 38 ..
5.237.d:
कृच्छ्रसेवी भवेद्यस्तु सुप्ते देवे जनार्दने ..
पापराशिं विनिर्धूय वैकुण्ठे गणतां व्रजेत् .. 38 ..
5.237.m: Whoever practices the Kṛcchra penance while God Janārdana is asleep, / shaking off the mass of sins, will attain status among the attendants in Vaikuṇṭha.

5.237.s:
taptakṛcchraparo yastu supte deve janārdane ..
kīrtiṃ saṃprāpya vā putraṃ viṣṇusāyujyatāṃ vrajet .. 39 ..
5.237.d:
तप्तकृच्छ्रपरो यस्तु सुप्ते देवे जनार्दने ..
कीर्तिं संप्राप्य वा पुत्रं विष्णुसायुज्यतां व्रजेत् .. 39 ..
5.237.m: Whoever is devoted to the Taptakṛcchra penance while God Janārdana is asleep, / having obtained renown or a son, will attain union with Viṣṇu.

5.237.s:
dugdhāhāraparo yastu cāturmāsye'bhijāyate ..
tasya pāpasahasrāṇi vilayaṃ yāṃti dehinaḥ .. 6.238.40 ..
5.237.d:
दुग्धाहारपरो यस्तु चातुर्मास्येऽभिजायते ..
तस्य पापसहस्राणि विलयं यांति देहिनः .. 6.238.40 ..
5.237.m: The embodied soul who becomes devoted to a milk diet during the Cāturmāsya, / thousands of his sins dissolve away.

5.237.s:
mitānnāśanakṛddhīraścāturmāsye naro yadi ..
nirdhūya sakalaṃ pāpaṃ vaikuṇṭhapadamāpnuyāt .. 41 ..
5.237.d:
मितान्नाशनकृद्धीरश्चातुर्मास्ये नरो यदि ..
निर्धूय सकलं पापं वैकुण्ठपदमाप्नुयात् .. 41 ..
5.237.m: If a wise man eats measured food during the Cāturmāsya, / having shaken off all sin, he will attain the abode of Vaikuṇṭha.

5.237.s:
ekānnāśanakṛnmartyo na rogairabhi bhūyate ..
akṣāralavaṇāśī ca cāturmāsye na pāpabhāk .. 42 ..
5.237.d:
एकान्नाशनकृन्मर्त्यो न रोगैरभि भूयते ..
अक्षारलवणाशी च चातुर्मास्ये न पापभाक् .. 42 ..
5.237.m: A mortal who eats only one meal a day is not overcome by diseases; / and one who eats food without pungent salts during the Cāturmāsya does not incur sin.

5.237.s:
kṛtāhāro mahāpāpairnirmukto jāyate dhruvam ..
harimuddiśya māseṣu caturṣu ca na saṃśayaḥ .. 43 ..
5.237.d:
कृताहारो महापापैर्निर्मुक्तो जायते ध्रुवम् ..
हरिमुद्दिश्य मासेषु चतुर्षु च न संशयः .. 43 ..
5.237.m: [Even one who has] taken [only such] food certainly becomes liberated from great sins / during the four months dedicated to Hari; there is no doubt.

5.237.s:
kandamūlāśanakaraḥ pūrvajānsaha cātmanā ..
uddhṛtya narakādghorādyāti viṣṇusalokatām .. 44 ..
5.237.d:
कन्दमूलाशनकरः पूर्वजान्सह चात्मना ..
उद्धृत्य नरकाद्घोराद्याति विष्णुसलोकताम् .. 44 ..
5.237.m: One who eats bulbs and roots, having delivered his ancestors together with himself / from the terrible hell, goes to the world of Viṣṇu.

5.237.s:
nityāṃbuprāśanakaraścāturmāsye yadā bhavet ..
dinedine'śvamedhasya phalamāpnotyasaṃśayam .. 45 ..
5.237.d:
नित्यांबुप्राशनकरश्चातुर्मास्ये यदा भवेत् ..
दिनेदिनेऽश्वमेधस्य फलमाप्नोत्यसंशयम् .. 45 ..
5.237.m: When one drinks only water daily during the Cāturmāsya, / day after day he undoubtedly obtains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice.

5.237.s:
śītavṛṣṭisaho yastu cāturmāsye naro bhavet ..
hariprītyai jagannāthastasyātmānaṃ prayacchati .. 46 ..
5.237.d:
शीतवृष्टिसहो यस्तु चातुर्मास्ये नरो भवेत् ..
हरिप्रीत्यै जगन्नाथस्तस्यात्मानं प्रयच्छति .. 46 ..
5.237.m: The man who endures cold and rain during the Cāturmāsya / for the pleasure of Hari, the Lord of the universe gives Himself to him.

5.237.s:
mahāpārākasaṃjñaṃ tu mahattapa udāhṛtam ..
māsaikamupavāsena sarvaṃ pūrṇaṃ prajāyate .. 47 ..
5.237.d:
महापाराकसंज्ञं तु महत्तप उदाहृतम् ..
मासैकमुपवासेन सर्वं पूर्णं प्रजायते .. 47 ..
5.237.m: The penance named Mahāpārāka is declared to be a great austerity; / by a single month of fasting, everything becomes complete.

5.237.s:
devasvāpadinādau tu yāvatpavitradvādaśī ..
pavitradvādaśīpūrvaṃ yāvacchravaṇadvādaśī .. 48 ..
5.237.d:
देवस्वापदिनादौ तु यावत्पवित्रद्वादशी ..
पवित्रद्वादशीपूर्वं यावच्छ्रवणद्वादशी .. 48 ..
5.237.m: From the first day of the God's sleep up to the Pavitra-dvādaśī; / [and from] before Pavitra-dvādaśī up to the Śravaṇa-dvādaśī:

5.237.s:
mahāpārākametaddhi dvitīyaṃ parikīrtitam ..
śravaṇadvādaśīpūrvaṃ prāptā cāśvinadvādaśī ..49..
5.237.d:
महापाराकमेतद्धि द्वितीयं परिकीर्तितम् ..
श्रवणद्वादशीपूर्वं प्राप्ता चाश्विनद्वादशी ..49..
5.237.m: this is indeed proclaimed as the second Mahāpārāka. / From before Śravaṇa-dvādaśī until the Āśvina-dvādaśī is reached:

5.237.s:
mahāpārāka tṛtīyaṃ prājñaiśca samudāhṛtam ..
āśvinadvādaśī cādau prāptā devasubodhinī .. 6.238.50 ..
5.237.d:
महापाराक तृतीयं प्राज्ञैश्च समुदाहृतम् ..
आश्विनद्वादशी चादौ प्राप्ता देवसुबोधिनी .. 6.238.50 ..
5.237.m: this is declared by the wise to be the third Mahāpārāka. / And from the Āśvina-dvādaśī first until the Devasubodhinī is reached:

5.237.s:
mahāpārākametaddhi caturthaṃ parikathyate ..
eteṣāmekamapi ca nārī vā puruṣo'pi vā .. 51 ..
5.237.d:
महापाराकमेतद्धि चतुर्थं परिकथ्यते ..
एतेषामेकमपि च नारी वा पुरुषोऽपि वा .. 51 ..
5.237.m: this is proclaimed as the fourth Mahāpārāka. / Even if [undertaking] just one of these, either a woman or a man

5.237.s:
yaḥ karoti naro bhaktyā sa ca viṣṇuḥ sanātanaḥ ..
idaṃ ca sarvatapasāṃ mahattapa udāhṛtam .. 52 ..
5.237.d:
यः करोति नरो भक्त्या स च विष्णुः सनातनः ..
इदं च सर्वतपसां महत्तप उदाहृतम् .. 52 ..
5.237.m: who performs it with devotion, that man becomes the eternal Viṣṇu. / And of all austerities, this is declared to be the greatest austerity.

5.237.s:
duṣkaraṃ durlabhaṃ loke cāturmāsye makhādhikam ..
divasedivase tasya yajñāyutaphalaṃ smṛtam .. 53 ..
5.237.d:
दुष्करं दुर्लभं लोके चातुर्मास्ये मखाधिकम् ..
दिवसेदिवसे तस्य यज्ञायुतफलं स्मृतम् .. 53 ..
5.237.m: It is difficult to perform, rare in the world, superior to sacrifices during the Cāturmāsya; / day after day, his fruit is remembered as equal to ten thousand sacrifices.

5.237.s:
mahattapa idaṃ yena kṛtaṃ jagati durlabham ..
idameva mahāpuṇyamidameva mahatsukham ..
idameva paraṃ śreyo mahāpārākasevanam .. 54 ..
5.237.d:
महत्तप इदं येन कृतं जगति दुर्लभम् ..
इदमेव महापुण्यमिदमेव महत्सुखम् ..
इदमेव परं श्रेयो महापाराकसेवनम् .. 54 ..
5.237.m: By whoever this great austerity, rare in the world, is performed: / this alone is great merit, this alone is great happiness, / this alone is supreme welfare—the observance of the Mahāpārāka.

5.237.s:
nārāyaṇo vaseddehe jñānaṃ tasya prajāyate ..
jīvanmuktaḥ sa bhavati mahāpātakakārakaḥ .. 55 ..
5.237.d:
नारायणो वसेद्देहे ज्ञानं तस्य प्रजायते ..
जीवन्मुक्तः स भवति महापातककारकः .. 55 ..
5.237.m: Nārāyaṇa will dwell in his body; knowledge is born in him; / [even if] a perpetrator of great sins, he becomes liberated while living.

5.237.s:
tāvadgarjaṃti pāpāni narakāstāvadeva hi ..
tāvanmāyāsahasrāṇi yāvanmāso pavāsakaḥ .. 56 ..
5.237.d:
तावद्गर्जंति पापानि नरकास्तावदेव हि ..
तावन्मायासहस्राणि यावन्मासो पवासकः .. 56 ..
5.237.m: Sins roar only so long, hells [threaten] only so long, / and thousands of illusions [persist] only so long, until one fasts for a month.

5.237.s:
cāturmāsyupavāsī yo yasya prāṃgaṇiko bhavet ..
so'pi hatyāsahasrāṇi tyaktvā niṣkalmaṣo bhavet .. 57 ..
5.237.d:
चातुर्मास्युपवासी यो यस्य प्रांगणिको भवेत् ..
सोऽपि हत्यासहस्राणि त्यक्त्वा निष्कल्मषो भवेत् .. 57 ..
5.237.m: One who fasts during the Cāturmāsya, in whose courtyard he may be, / even he, casting off thousands of killings, becomes free from defilement.

5.237.s: ya idaṃ śrāvayenmartyo yaḥ paṭhetsatataṃ svayam .. 58 ..
5.237.d: य इदं श्रावयेन्मर्त्यो यः पठेत्सततं स्वयम् .. 58 ..
5.237.m: A mortal who causes this to be heard, or who constantly recites it himself,

5.237.s: so'pi vācaspatisamaḥ phalaṃ prāpnotyasaṃśayam .. 59 ..
5.237.d: सोऽपि वाचस्पतिसमः फलं प्राप्नोत्यसंशयम् .. 59 ..
5.237.m: he too, equal to Vācaspati, undoubtedly obtains the fruit.

5.237.s:
idaṃ purāṇaṃ paramaṃ pavitraṃ śṛṇvangṛṇanpāpaviśuddhihetu ..
nārāyaṇaṃ taṃ manasā vicintya mṛto'bhigacchatyamṛtaṃ surādhikam .. 6.238.60 ..
5.237.d:
इदं पुराणं परमं पवित्रं शृण्वन्गृणन्पापविशुद्धिहेतु ..
नारायणं तं मनसा विचिन्त्य मृतोऽभिगच्छत्यमृतं सुराधिकम् .. 6.238.60 ..
5.237.m: Hearing or reciting this supreme, pure Purāṇa, which is the cause of purification from sin, / contemplating that Nārāyaṇa in the mind, when dead he attains immortality, superior to the gods.

5.237.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsyamāhātmye tapomahimāvarṇanaṃ nāmāṣṭatriṃśaduttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 238 ..
5.237.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये तपोमहिमावर्णनं नामाष्टत्रिंशदुत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः .. 238 ..
5.237.m: Thus ends the two hundred and thirty-eighth chapter, named 'Description of the Greatness of Austerity' in the praise of Cāturmāsya, in the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada, in the narrative of Śeṣaśāyin, in the praise of Hāṭakeśvara-kṣetra, in the sixth Nāgarakhaṇḍa in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.238.s:
.. nārada uvāca ..
upacāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ pūjanaṃ kriyate katham ..
te ke ṣoḍaśa bhāvāḥ syurnityaṃ ye śayane hareḥ .. 1 ..
5.238.d:
.. नारद उवाच ..
उपचारैः षोडशभिः पूजनं क्रियते कथम् ..
ते के षोडश भावाः स्युर्नित्यं ये शयने हरेः .. 1 ..
5.238.m: Nārada said: / How is worship performed with the sixteen offerings? / What are those sixteen devotional states that are constantly [observed] during Hari's sleep?

5.238.s:
etadvistarato brūhi pṛcchato me prajāpate ..
tava prasādamāsādya jagatpūjyo bhavāmyaham .. 2 ..
5.238.d:
एतद्विस्तरतो ब्रूहि पृच्छतो मे प्रजापते ..
तव प्रसादमासाद्य जगत्पूज्यो भवाम्यहम् .. 2 ..
5.238.m: Speak this in detail to me as I ask, O Prajāpati. / Having attained your grace, I shall become worthy of worship by the world.

5.238.s:
.. brahmovāca .. ..
viṣṇubhaktirdṛḍhā kāryā vedaśāstravidhānataḥ ..
vedamūlamidaṃ sarvaṃ vedo viṣṇuḥ sanātanaḥ .. 3 ..
5.238.d:
.. ब्रह्मोवाच .. ..
विष्णुभक्तिर्दृढा कार्या वेदशास्त्रविधानतः ..
वेदमूलमिदं सर्वं वेदो विष्णुः सनातनः .. 3 ..
5.238.m: Brahmā said: / Firm devotion to Viṣṇu should be cultivated according to the rule of the Vedas and treatises. / All this has the Veda as its root; eternal Viṣṇu is the Veda.

5.238.s:
te vedā brāhmaṇādhārā brāhmaṇāścāgnidaivatāḥ ..
agnau prāstāhutirvipro yajñe devaṃ yajansadā .. 4 ..
5.238.d:
ते वेदा ब्राह्मणाधारा ब्राह्मणाश्चाग्निदैवताः ..
अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतिर्विप्रो यज्ञे देवं यजन्सदा .. 4 ..
5.238.m: Those Vedas rest upon brahmins, and brahmins have fire as their deity. / The brahmin whose oblation is cast into the fire, always worshipping the deity in the sacrifice,

5.238.s:
jagatsaṃdhārayetsarvaṃ viṣṇupūjārataḥ sadā ..
nārāyaṇaḥ smṛto dhyātaḥ kleśaduḥkhādināśanaḥ .. 5 ..
5.238.d:
जगत्संधारयेत्सर्वं विष्णुपूजारतः सदा ..
नारायणः स्मृतो ध्यातः क्लेशदुःखादिनाशनः .. 5 ..
5.238.m: sustains the entire world, ever delighting in the worship of Viṣṇu. / Nārāyaṇa, remembered and meditated upon, is the destroyer of distress, sorrow, and other ills.

5.238.s:
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa jalarūpagato hariḥ ..
jalādannāni jāyaṃte jagatāṃ tṛptihetave .. 6 ..
5.238.d:
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण जलरूपगतो हरिः ..
जलादन्नानि जायंते जगतां तृप्तिहेतवे .. 6 ..
5.238.m: Especially during the Cāturmāsya, Hari enters the form of water. / From water foods are produced to satisfy the worlds.

5.238.s:
viṣṇudehāṃśasaṃbhūtaṃ tadannaṃ brahma iṣyate ..
tadannaṃ viṣṇave dattvā hyāvāhanapuraḥsaram .. 7 ..
5.238.d:
विष्णुदेहांशसंभूतं तदन्नं ब्रह्म इष्यते ..
तदन्नं विष्णवे दत्त्वा ह्यावाहनपुरःसरम् .. 7 ..
5.238.m: Born from a portion of Viṣṇu's body, that food is regarded as Brahman. / Having offered that food to Viṣṇu, preceded indeed by invocation,

5.238.s:
punarjanmajarākleśasaṃskārairnābhibhūyate ..
ākāśasaṃbhavo veda eka eva purā'bhavat .. 8 ..
5.238.d:
पुनर्जन्मजराक्लेशसंस्कारैर्नाभिभूयते ..
आकाशसंभवो वेद एक एव पुराऽभवत् .. 8 ..
5.238.m: one is not overpowered by the impressions of rebirth, old age, and suffering. / In the beginning there was only a single Veda, originating from space.

5.238.s:
tato yajuḥsāmasaṃjñāmṛgvedaḥ prāpa bhūtaye ..
ṛgvedo'bhihitaḥ pūrvaṃ yajuḥsahasraśīrṣeti ca .. 9 ..
5.238.d:
ततो यजुःसामसंज्ञामृग्वेदः प्राप भूतये ..
ऋग्वेदोऽभिहितः पूर्वं यजुःसहस्रशीर्षेति च .. 9 ..
5.238.m: Then the Ṛgveda obtained the designations of Yajus and Sāman for prosperity. / The Ṛgveda was stated first, and the Yajus begins with 'Thousand-headed' [sahasraśīrṣā].

5.238.s:
ṣoḍaśarcaṃ mahāsūktaṃ nārāyaṇamayaṃ param ..
tasyāpi pāṭhamātreṇa brahmahatyā niva rtate..6.239.10...
5.238.d:
षोडशर्चं महासूक्तं नारायणमयं परम् ..
तस्यापि पाठमात्रेण ब्रह्महत्या निव र्तते..6.239.10...
5.238.m: This supreme great hymn of sixteen verses consists entirely of Nārāyaṇa. / Even by merely reciting it, the sin of killing a brahmin ceases.

5.238.s:
vipraḥ pūrvaṃ nyaseddehe smṛtyuktena nije budhaḥ..
tatastu pratimāyāṃ ca śālagrāme viśeṣataḥ..11..
5.238.d:
विप्रः पूर्वं न्यसेद्देहे स्मृत्युक्तेन निजे बुधः..
ततस्तु प्रतिमायां च शालग्रामे विशेषतः..11..
5.238.m: A wise brahmin should first perform the ritual placement upon his own body as prescribed in the Smṛti, / and then upon the image, especially upon a śālagrāma stone.

5.238.s:
krameṇa ca tataḥ kuryātpaścādāvāhanādikam..
āvāhya sakalaṃ rūpaṃ vaikuṇṭhasthānasaṃsthitam..12..
5.238.d:
क्रमेण च ततः कुर्यात्पश्चादावाहनादिकम्..
आवाह्य सकलं रूपं वैकुण्ठस्थानसंस्थितम्..12..
5.238.m: Thereafter he should carry out invocation and the other rites in due order, / having invoked the complete form residing in the realm of Vaikuṇṭha,

5.238.s:
kaustubhena virājaṃtaṃ sūryakoṭisamaprabham..
daṃḍahastaṃ śikhāsūtrasahitaṃ pītavāsasam ..13..
5.238.d:
कौस्तुभेन विराजंतं सूर्यकोटिसमप्रभम्..
दंडहस्तं शिखासूत्रसहितं पीतवाससम् ..13..
5.238.m: shining with the Kaustubha gem, equal in splendour to ten million suns, / holding a staff in hand, accompanied by topknot and sacred thread, clad in yellow garments.

5.238.s:
mahāsaṃnyāsinaṃ dhyāyeccāturmāsye viśeṣataḥ ..
evaṃ rūpamayaṃ viṣṇuṃ sarvapāpaughahāriṇam ..14..
5.238.d:
महासंन्यासिनं ध्यायेच्चातुर्मास्ये विशेषतः ..
एवं रूपमयं विष्णुं सर्वपापौघहारिणम् ..14..
5.238.m: Especially during the Cāturmāsya, one should meditate upon Him as the great ascetic— / Viṣṇu in this form, who takes away the flood of all sins.

5.238.s:
āvāhayecca purato dhyānasaṃsthaṃ dvijottama..
ṛcā prathamayā cāsyoṃkārādisamudīrṇayā ..15..
5.238.d:
आवाहयेच्च पुरतो ध्यानसंस्थं द्विजोत्तम..
ऋचा प्रथमया चास्योंकारादिसमुदीर्णया ..15..
5.238.m: And one should invoke before oneself Him who is fixed in meditation, O best of the twice-born, / with the first verse uttered along with the syllable Om and the rest.

5.238.s:
dvitīyayā cāsanaṃ ca pārṣadaiśca samanvitam..
sauvarṇānyāsanānyeṣāṃ manasā paricintayet ..16..
5.238.d:
द्वितीयया चासनं च पार्षदैश्च समन्वितम्..
सौवर्णान्यासनान्येषां मनसा परिचिन्तयेत् ..16..
5.238.m: With the second [verse he should offer] a seat, accompanied by His attendants; / in his mind he should imagine golden seats for them.

5.238.s:
cintanairbhaktiyogena paripūrṇaṃ ca tadbhavet ..
pādyaṃ tṛtīyayā kāryaṃ gaṃgāṃ tatra smaredbudhaḥ .. 17 ..
5.238.d:
चिन्तनैर्भक्तियोगेन परिपूर्णं च तद्भवेत् ..
