5.242.m: Brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and likewise virtuous Śūdras / have the right to the Śāligrāma, but others never do. 45

5.242.s:
.. sacchūdra uvāca .. ..
brahmanvedavidāṃ śreṣṭha sarvaśāstraviśārada ..
strīśūdrādiniṣedho'yaṃ śāligrāme hi śrūyate .. 46 ..
5.242.d:
.. सच्छूद्र उवाच .. ..
ब्रह्मन्वेदविदां श्रेष्ठ सर्वशास्त्रविशारद ..
स्त्रीशूद्रादिनिषेधोऽयं शालिग्रामे हि श्रूयते .. 46 ..
5.242.m: The virtuous Śūdra said: / O brahmin, best of Vedic knowers, skilled in all sacred treatises! / A prohibition regarding women, Śūdras, and others is indeed heard concerning the Śāligrāma. 46

5.242.s: mādṛśastvaṃ kathaṃ śāligrāmapūjāvidhiṃ vada .. 47 ..
5.242.d: मादृशस्त्वं कथं शालिग्रामपूजाविधिं वद .. 47 ..
5.242.m: Tell how one like me may perform the ritual of worship for the Śāligrāma. 47

5.242.s:
.. gālava uvāca .. ..
asacchūdragataṃ dāsa niṣedhaṃ viddhi mānada ..
strīṇāmapi ca sādhvīnāṃ naivābhāvaḥ prakīrtitaḥ .. 48 ..
5.242.d:
.. गालव उवाच .. ..
असच्छूद्रगतं दास निषेधं विद्धि मानद ..
स्त्रीणामपि च साध्वीनां नैवाभावः प्रकीर्तितः .. 48 ..
5.242.m: Gālava said: / O servant, knower of honor, know that the prohibition applies to unvirtuous Śūdras; / nor is there stated to be an exclusion of virtuous women. 48

5.242.s:
mā bhūtsaṃśayastenātra nā''pnuṣe saṃśayātphalam ..
śāligrāmārcanaparāḥ śuddhadehā vivekinaḥ .. 49 ..
5.242.d:
मा भूत्संशयस्तेनात्र ना'ऽप्नुषे संशयात्फलम् ..
शालिग्रामार्चनपराः शुद्धदेहा विवेकिनः .. 49 ..
5.242.m: Let there be no doubt in you about this; one does not obtain the fruit [of rites] through doubt. / Those devoted to the worship of the Śāligrāma, of pure body and possessing discernment, 49

5.242.s:
na te yamapuraṃ yāṃti cāturmāsye ca pūjakāḥ ..
śāligrāmārpitaṃ mālyaṃ śirasā dhārayaṃti ye .. 6.243.50 ..
5.242.d:
न ते यमपुरं यांति चातुर्मास्ये च पूजकाः ..
शालिग्रामार्पितं माल्यं शिरसा धारयंति ये .. 6.243.50 ..
5.242.m: do not go to the city of Yama; and those who worship during the Cāturmāsya, / who wear upon their heads a garland offered to the Śāligrāma, 50

5.242.s:
teṣāṃ pāpasahasrāṇi vilayaṃ yāṃti tatkṣaṇāt..
śāligrāma śilāgre tu ye prayacchaṃti dīpakam .. 51 ..
5.242.d:
तेषां पापसहस्राणि विलयं यांति तत्क्षणात्..
शालिग्राम शिलाग्रे तु ये प्रयच्छंति दीपकम् .. 51 ..
5.242.m: their thousands of sins dissolve in that very instant. / Those who offer a lamp before the Śāligrāma stone, 51

5.242.s:
teṣāṃ saurapure vāsaḥ kadācinnaiva hīyate ..
śāligrāmagataṃ viṣṇuṃ sumanobhirmanoharaiḥ..
ye'rcayaṃti mahāśūdra supte deve harau tathā .. 52 ..
5.242.d:
तेषां सौरपुरे वासः कदाचिन्नैव हीयते ..
शालिग्रामगतं विष्णुं सुमनोभिर्मनोहरैः..
येऽर्चयंति महाशूद्र सुप्ते देवे हरौ तथा .. 52 ..
5.242.m: their residence in the solar city is never lost. / O great Śūdra, those who worship Viṣṇu residing in the Śāligrāma with charming flowers / while Lord Hari is asleep [during the rains], 52

5.242.s:
paṃcāmṛtena snapanaṃ ye kurvaṃti sadā narāḥ ..
śāligrāmaśilāyāṃ ca na te saṃsāriṇo narāḥ.. 53 ..
5.242.d:
पंचामृतेन स्नपनं ये कुर्वंति सदा नराः ..
शालिग्रामशिलायां च न ते संसारिणो नराः.. 53 ..
5.242.m: and those men who constantly perform the ceremonial bath with the five nectars / upon the Śāligrāma stone, are men bound no longer to transmigration. 53

5.242.s:
mukternidānamamalaṃ śāligrāmagataṃ harim ..
hṛdi nyasya sadā bhaktyā yo dhyāyati sa muktibhāk .. 54 ..
5.242.d:
मुक्तेर्निदानममलं शालिग्रामगतं हरिम् ..
हृदि न्यस्य सदा भक्त्या यो ध्यायति स मुक्तिभाक् .. 54 ..
5.242.m: He who, having placed Hari residing in the Śāligrāma, the spotless cause of liberation, / in his heart, always meditates on Him with devotion, becomes a sharer in liberation. 54

5.242.s:
tulasīdalajāṃ mālāṃ śāligrāmopari nyaset ..
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa sarvakāmānavāpnuyāt .. 55 ..
5.242.d:
तुलसीदलजां मालां शालिग्रामोपरि न्यसेत् ..
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण सर्वकामानवाप्नुयात् .. 55 ..
5.242.m: One should place a garland made of tulasī leaves upon the Śāligrāma; / especially during the Cāturmāsya, one will obtain all desires. 55

5.242.s:
na tāvatpuṣpajā mālā śāligrāmasya vallabhā ..
sarvadā tulasī devī viṣṇornityaṃ śubhā priyā .. .. 56 ..
5.242.d:
न तावत्पुष्पजा माला शालिग्रामस्य वल्लभा ..
सर्वदा तुलसी देवी विष्णोर्नित्यं शुभा प्रिया .. .. 56 ..
5.242.m: A garland made of flowers is not so dear to the Śāligrāma; / the goddess Tulasī is always auspicious and dear to Viṣṇu. 56

5.242.s:
tulasī vallabhā nityaṃ cāturmāsye viśeṣataḥ ..
śāligrāmo mahāviṣṇustulasī śrīrna saṃśayaḥ .. 57 ..
5.242.d:
तुलसी वल्लभा नित्यं चातुर्मास्ये विशेषतः ..
शालिग्रामो महाविष्णुस्तुलसी श्रीर्न संशयः .. 57 ..
5.242.m: Tulasī is always beloved, especially during the Cāturmāsya; / the Śāligrāma is Mahāviṣṇu, and Tulasī is Śrī, without doubt. 57

5.242.s:
ato vāsitapānīyaiḥ snāpyaṃ caṃdanacarcitaiḥ ..
maṃjarībhiryutaṃ devaṃ śālagrāmaśilāharim .. 58 ..
5.242.d:
अतो वासितपानीयैः स्नाप्यं चंदनचर्चितैः ..
मंजरीभिर्युतं देवं शालग्रामशिलाहरिम् .. 58 ..
5.242.m: Therefore, having bathed the god, Hari in the Śāligrāma stone, / with perfumed waters smeared with sandalwood, accompanied by blossom-spikes, 58

5.242.s:
tulasīsaṃbhavābhiśca kṛtvā kāmānavāpnuyāt ..
patre tu prathame brahmā dvitīye bhagavāñchivaḥ .. 59 ..
5.242.d:
तुलसीसंभवाभिश्च कृत्वा कामानवाप्नुयात् ..
पत्रे तु प्रथमे ब्रह्मा द्वितीये भगवाञ्छिवः .. 59 ..
5.242.m: and with those born of tulasī, one will obtain one's desires. / In the first leaf is Brahmā, and in the second is Lord Śiva; 59

5.242.s:
maṃjaryāṃ bhagavānviṣṇustadekasthatrayā sadā ..
maṃjarī dalasaṃyuktā grāhyā budhajanaiḥ śubhā .. 6.243.60 ..
5.242.d:
मंजर्यां भगवान्विष्णुस्तदेकस्थत्रया सदा ..
मंजरी दलसंयुक्ता ग्राह्या बुधजनैः शुभा .. 6.243.60 ..
5.242.m: in the blossom-spike is Lord Viṣṇu; thus the triad always resides in one place. / An auspicious blossom-spike joined with leaves should be taken by wise men. 60

5.242.s:
tāṃ nivedya gurau bhaktyā janmādikṣayakāraṇam ..
śāligrāme dhūparāśiṃ nivedya haritatparaḥ .. 61 ..
5.242.d:
तां निवेद्य गुरौ भक्त्या जन्मादिक्षयकारणम् ..
शालिग्रामे धूपराशिं निवेद्य हरितत्परः .. 61 ..
5.242.m: Having offered it with devotion to the guru—the cause of the destruction of rebirth and [other ills]— / and having offered an abundance of incense to the Śāligrāma, devoted to Hari, 61

5.242.s:
cāturmāsye viśeṣeṇa manuṣyo naiva nārakī..
śāligrāmaṃ naro dṛṣṭvā pūjitaṃ kusumaiḥ śubhaiḥ .. 62 ..
5.242.d:
चातुर्मास्ये विशेषेण मनुष्यो नैव नारकी..
शालिग्रामं नरो दृष्ट्वा पूजितं कुसुमैः शुभैः .. 62 ..
5.242.m: especially during the Cāturmāsya, a human being never goes to hell. / A man having beheld the Śāligrāma worshipped with auspicious flowers, 62

5.242.s:
sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā yāti tanmayatāṃ harau ..
ya stautyaśmagataṃ viṣṇuṃ gaṃḍakījalasaṃbhavam .. 63 ..
5.242.d:
सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा याति तन्मयतां हरौ ..
य स्तौत्यश्मगतं विष्णुं गंडकीजलसंभवम् .. 63 ..
5.242.m: his soul purified of all sins, attains oneness with Hari. / He who praises Viṣṇu present in the stone born from the waters of the Gaṇḍakī 63

5.242.s:
śrutismṛtipurāṇaiśca so'pi viṣṇupadaṃ vrajet ..
śāligrāmaśilāyāśca caturviṃśatisaṃkhyakāḥ ..
bhedāḥ saṃti mahāśūdra tāñchṛṇuṣva mahāmate .. 64 ..
5.242.d:
श्रुतिस्मृतिपुराणैश्च सोऽपि विष्णुपदं व्रजेत् ..
शालिग्रामशिलायाश्च चतुर्विंशतिसंख्यकाः ..
भेदाः संति महाशूद्र ताञ्छृणुष्व महामते .. 64 ..
5.242.m: by means of the Śrutis, Smṛtis, and Purāṇas, he too goes to the abode of Viṣṇu. / O great Śūdra, the varieties of the Śāligrāma stone / are twenty-four in number; hear them, O high-minded one. 64

5.242.s:
imāḥ pūjyāśca loke'tra caturviṃśatisaṃkhyakāḥ ..
tāsāṃ ca daivataṃ viṣṇuṃ nāmāni ca vadāmyaham .. 65 ..
5.242.d:
इमाः पूज्याश्च लोकेऽत्र चतुर्विंशतिसंख्यकाः ..
तासां च दैवतं विष्णुं नामानि च वदाम्यहम् .. 65 ..
5.242.m: These twenty-four in number are worthy of worship in this world; / I shall proclaim their deity Viṣṇu and their names. 65

5.242.s:
sa eva mūrttaścaturuttarāsirviṃśadbhireko bhagavānyathā''dyaḥ ..
sa eva saṃvatsaranāmasaṃjñaḥ sa eva grāvāgata ādidevaḥ .. 66 ..
5.242.d:
स एव मूर्त्तश्चतुरुत्तरासिर्विंशद्भिरेको भगवान्यथा'ऽद्यः ..
स एव संवत्सरनामसंज्ञः स एव ग्रावागत आदिदेवः .. 66 ..
5.242.m: The primordial, singular Lord is manifest as four plus twenty; / He is known by the names of the year, He is the primeval God present in the stone. 66

5.242.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetra māhātmye śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsyamāhātmye paijavanopākhyāne śāligrāmapūjanamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma tricatvāriṃśatyuttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 243 ..
5.242.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्र माहात्म्ये शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये पैजवनोपाख्याने शालिग्रामपूजनमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम त्रिचत्वारिंशत्युत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः .. 243 ..
5.242.m: Thus ends the two hundred forty-third chapter, entitled 'Description of the Glory of Worshipping the Śāligrāma', in the episode of Paijavana, in the Glory of Cāturmāsya, in the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada, in the story of Śeṣaśāyin, in the Glory of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the sixth Nāgarakhaṇḍa of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. 243

5.243.s:
.. paijavana uvāca .. ..
etānbhedānmama brūhi vistareṇa tapodhana ..
tvadvākyāmṛtapānena tṛṣā naiva praśāmyati .. 1 ..
5.243.d:
.. पैजवन उवाच .. ..
एतान्भेदान्मम ब्रूहि विस्तरेण तपोधन ..
त्वद्वाक्यामृतपानेन तृषा नैव प्रशाम्यति .. 1 ..
5.243.m: Paijavana said: / O you whose wealth is austerity, declare these varieties to me in detail; / drinking the nectar of your speech, my thirst is not at all quenched. 1

5.243.s:
.. gālava uvāca .. ..
śṛṇu vistarato bhedānpurāṇoktānvadāmi te ..
yāñchrutvā mucyate'vaśyaṃ manujaḥ sarvakilbiṣāt .. 2 ..
5.243.d:
.. गालव उवाच .. ..
शृणु विस्तरतो भेदान्पुराणोक्तान्वदामि ते ..
याञ्छ्रुत्वा मुच्यतेऽवश्यं मनुजः सर्वकिल्बिषात् .. 2 ..
5.243.m: Gālava said: / Listen in detail, I shall tell you the varieties spoken of in the Purāṇas, / hearing which a human being is inevitably freed from all sins. 2

5.243.s:
pūrvaṃ tu keśavaḥ pūjyo dvitīyo madhusūdanaḥ ..
saṃkarṣaṇastṛtīyastu tato dāmodaraḥ smṛtaḥ .. 3 ..
5.243.d:
पूर्वं तु केशवः पूज्यो द्वितीयो मधुसूदनः ..
संकर्षणस्तृतीयस्तु ततो दामोदरः स्मृतः .. 3 ..
5.243.m: First Keśava is to be worshipped, the second is Madhusūdana, / the third is Saṃkarṣaṇa, and then Dāmodara is remembered. 3

5.243.s:
paṃcamo vāsudevākhyaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ pradyumnasaṃjñakaḥ ..
saptamo viṣṇuruktaścāṣṭamo mādhava eva ca .. 4 ..
5.243.d:
पंचमो वासुदेवाख्यः षष्ठः प्रद्युम्नसंज्ञकः ..
सप्तमो विष्णुरुक्तश्चाष्टमो माधव एव च .. 4 ..
5.243.m: The fifth is named Vāsudeva, the sixth is named Pradyumna, / the seventh is declared as Viṣṇu, and the eighth is Mādhava. 4

5.243.s:
navamo'naṃtamūrttiśca daśamaḥ puruṣottamaḥ ..
adhokṣajastataḥ paścāddvādaśastu janārdanaḥ .. 5 ..
5.243.d:
नवमोऽनंतमूर्त्तिश्च दशमः पुरुषोत्तमः ..
अधोक्षजस्ततः पश्चाद्द्वादशस्तु जनार्दनः .. 5 ..
5.243.m: The ninth is Anantamūrti, and the tenth is Puruṣottama; / thereafter Adhokṣaja, and the twelfth is Janārdana. 5

5.243.s:
trayodaśastu goviṃdaścaturdaśastrivikramaḥ ..
śrīdharaśca paṃcadaśo hṛṣīkeśastu ṣoḍaśaḥ .. 6 ..
5.243.d:
त्रयोदशस्तु गोविंदश्चतुर्दशस्त्रिविक्रमः ..
श्रीधरश्च पंचदशो हृषीकेशस्तु षोडशः .. 6 ..
5.243.m: The thirteenth is Govinda, the fourteenth is Trivikrama, / the fifteenth is Śrīdhara, and the sixteenth is Hṛṣīkeśa. 6

5.243.s:
nṛsiṃhastu saptadaśo viśvayonistataḥ param..
vāmanaśca tataḥ prokta stato nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 7 ..
5.243.d:
नृसिंहस्तु सप्तदशो विश्वयोनिस्ततः परम्..
वामनश्च ततः प्रोक्त स्ततो नारायणः स्मृतः .. 7 ..
5.243.m: The seventeenth is Nṛsiṃha, after that Viśvayoni; / then Vāmana is proclaimed, after that Nārāyaṇa is remembered. 7

5.243.s:
puṃḍarīkākṣa uktastu hyupeṃdraśca tataḥ param ..
haristrayoviṃśatimaḥ kṛṣṇaścāṃtya udāhṛtaḥ .. 9 ..
śāligrāmasya bhedāṃśca mayoktāstava śūdraja ..
mūrtibhedāstathā proktā eta eva mahādhana .. 9 ..
5.243.d:
पुंडरीकाक्ष उक्तस्तु ह्युपेंद्रश्च ततः परम् ..
हरिस्त्रयोविंशतिमः कृष्णश्चांत्य उदाहृतः .. 9 ..
शालिग्रामस्य भेदांश्च मयोक्तास्तव शूद्रज ..
मूर्तिभेदास्तथा प्रोक्ता एत एव महाधन .. 9 ..
5.243.m:
Puṇḍarīkākṣa is spoken of, and then indeed Upendra after that; / Hari is the twenty-third, and Kṛṣṇa is declared as the last. 8
These varieties of the Śāligrāma have been declared to you by me, O born of a Śūdra; / likewise, O wealthy one, these very manifestations of the deity are proclaimed. 9

5.243.s:
mūrttayastithinānmyaḥ syurekādaśyaḥ sadaiva hi ..
saṃvatsareṇa pūjyaṃte caturviṃśa timūrtayaḥ .. 6.244.10 ..
5.243.d:
मूर्त्तयस्तिथिनान्म्यः स्युरेकादश्यः सदैव हि ..
संवत्सरेण पूज्यंते चतुर्विंश तिमूर्तयः .. 6.244.10 ..
5.243.m: The forms are always named after the lunar days of the Ekādaśīs; / throughout the course of a year, the twenty-four forms are worshipped. 10

5.243.s:
devāvatārāśca tathā caturviṃśatisaṃkhyakāḥ ..
māsā mārgaśirādyāśca māsārddhāḥ pakṣasaṃjñakāḥ .. 11 ..
5.243.d:
देवावताराश्च तथा चतुर्विंशतिसंख्यकाः ..
मासा मार्गशिराद्याश्च मासार्द्धाः पक्षसंज्ञकाः .. 11 ..
5.243.m: And likewise the divine incarnations are twenty-four in number, / as are the months beginning with Mārgaśīrṣa, and the half-months known as fortnights.
Always worshiping them along with their presiding lords, one becomes full of devotion. / Thus the fourfold set consisting of twenty-four each has been declared.

5.243.s:
etaccatuṣṭayaṃ nṛṇāṃ dharmakāmārthamokṣadam ..
yaḥ śṛṇoti naro bhakttayā paṭhedvāpi samāhitaḥ .. 13 ..
5.243.d:
एतच्चतुष्टयं नृणां धर्मकामार्थमोक्षदम् ..
यः शृणोति नरो भक्त्तया पठेद्वापि समाहितः .. 13 ..
5.243.m: This tetrad bestows righteousness, pleasure, wealth, and liberation upon men. / A person who hears it with devotion, or recites it with concentrated mind—
Hari, the protector of the creation of living beings, becomes pleased with him.

5.243.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmya śeṣaśāyyupākhyāne brahmanāradasaṃvāde cāturmāsyamāhātmye śāligrāmaśilāsumūrttyutpattivarṇanaṃnāma catuścatvāriṃśaduttaradvi śatatamodhyāyaḥ .. 244 ..
5.243.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्य शेषशाय्युपाख्याने ब्रह्मनारदसंवादे चातुर्मास्यमाहात्म्ये शालिग्रामशिलासुमूर्त्त्युत्पत्तिवर्णनंनाम चतुश्चत्वारिंशदुत्तरद्वि शततमोध्यायः .. 244 ..
5.243.m: Thus ends the two hundred and forty-fourth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Origin of the Images in the Śāligrāma Stones,' in the Māhātmya of Cāturmāsya, in the Dialogue of Brahmā and Nārada, within the Story of Śeṣaśāyin, in the Māhātmya of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section], in the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
